149	/-! ## The finite chart adaptation -/
150	
151	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
152	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
153	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)
154	
155	/-- **The `Fin`-indexed basic-open cover data** of the two pinned charts of the relative
156	curve (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1a): `m₀ + m₁` basic-open generators with partition
157	witnesses. The DAT-1 datum `BasicOpenCoverData` carries `Type u` index fields and hence
158	lives in `Type (u+1)`; this `Fin`-indexed form is the `Type u` carrier a functor value
159	can quotient. -/
160	structure FinCoverData [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
161	  /-- The number of chart-0 pieces. -/
162	  m₀ : ℕ
163	  /-- The number of chart-1 pieces. -/
164	  m₁ : ℕ
165	  /-- The chart-0 basic-open generators. -/
166	  h₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
167	  /-- The chart-1 basic-open generators. -/
168	  h₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
169	  /-- The chart-0 partition coefficients. -/
170	  a₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
171	  /-- The chart-1 partition coefficients. -/
172	  a₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
173	  /-- The chart-0 partition witness. -/
174	  partition₀ : ∑ j : Fin m₀, a₀ j * h₀ j = 1
175	  /-- The chart-1 partition witness. -/
176	  partition₁ : ∑ j : Fin m₁, a₁ j * h₁ j = 1
177	
178	namespace FinCoverData
179	
180	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)
181	
182	/-- The gluing index of the adaptation, `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁`. -/
183	abbrev index : Type := Fin D.m₀ ⊕ Fin D.m₁
184	
185	/-- The pieces: the basic opens `D(h_j)` of the two pinned charts. -/
186	noncomputable def pieces : D.index → (relCurve C R).Opens :=
187	  Sum.elim (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j))
188	    (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j))
189	
190	@[simp]
191	lemma pieces_inl (j : Fin D.m₀) :
192	    D.pieces (Sum.inl j) = (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j) := rfl
193	
194	@[simp]
195	lemma pieces_inr (j : Fin D.m₁) :
196	    D.pieces (Sum.inr j) = (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j) := rfl
197	
198	/-- The chart-0 pieces cover the pinned chart `V₀ᴿ`. -/
199	lemma cover₀ : (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ≤
200	    ⨆ j : Fin D.m₀, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j) :=
201	  le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one D.a₀ D.h₀ D.partition₀
202	
203	/-- The chart-1 pieces cover the pinned chart `V₁ᴿ`. -/
204	lemma cover₁ : (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤
205	    ⨆ j : Fin D.m₁, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j) :=
206	  le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one D.a₁ D.h₁ D.partition₁
207	
208	end FinCoverData
209	
210	/-- Restriction of sections of the relative curve as an `R`-algebra homomorphism
211	(`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` structures on both sides). -/
212	noncomputable def relResAlgHom {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) :
213	    Γ(relCurve C R, V) →ₐ[R] Γ(relCurve C R, W) :=
214	  AlgHom.mk' (CommRingCat.Hom.hom ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op))
215	    (fun c x => by
216	      simp only [Algebra.smul_def]
217	      rw [map_mul]
218	      congr 1
219	      rw [Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra, Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra]
220	      exact (relCurve C R).overAlgebraMap_apply_res R (homOfLE h).op c)
221	
222	@[simp]
223	lemma relResAlgHom_apply {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) (s : Γ(relCurve C R, V)) :
224	    relResAlgHom C R h s = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom s :=
225	  rfl
226	
227	/-- **The finite chart adaptation of a local-equation system** (worksheet §1.1 (D1)):
228	basic-open cover data of the two pinned charts, equations `f_j` on the pieces, and the
229	pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel` — on the overlap of each piece with any member of
230	`d.cover`, `f_j` agrees with `d`'s equation up to a unit. Regularity of the `f_j` is
231	DERIVED (`DivisorAdaptation.eqn_regular`), not stored. -/
232	structure DivisorAdaptation [IsAffineHom π] (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
233	    Type u extends FinCoverData C R π where
234	  /-- The equation on the piece `D(h_j)`. -/
235	  eqn : ∀ j : toFinCoverData.index, Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j)
236	  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units: on the overlap of each piece with
237	  any member of `d`'s cover, `f_j` and `d`'s equation differ by a unit. Point-free (the
238	  `DivEq` spelling), so it pulls back along arbitrary morphisms — the resolution of the
239	  DD-1 pt-transport seam (`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §1a). The quantifier ranges over ALL
240	  `y`: the empty overlap carries the zero ring, where the clause is trivial. -/
241	  eqn_rel : ∀ (j : toFinCoverData.index) (y : relCurve C R),
242	    ∃ u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ,
243	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
244	        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
245	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)
246	
247	namespace DivisorAdaptation
248	
249	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}

7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarSwallow
8	
9	/-!
10	# A connected divisor can be certified only inside a single pinned chart
11	
12	The two preceding files bracket the certificate assembler's per-piece no-leak clause:
13	`DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` shows it forces the chart traces `supportLocus ∩ V_b` to
14	be closed, and `DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean` shows the "swallow or miss" shape produces it.
15	This file closes the bracket, and thereby decides the lane's satisfiability question.
16	
17	The observation is that leak-freeness *plus connectedness of the divisor* already implies
18	swallow-or-miss.  For each piece the trace `supportLocus ∩ pieces j` is open in the support
19	(the piece is open) and closed in it (that is leak-freeness), so a connected support leaves
20	only the two degenerate values: the trace is empty, or it is everything.  Feeding this into
21	the chart dichotomies of `DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean` and `relCover_sup` gives
22	
23	> **a connected divisor whose adaptation is leak-free at every piece lies inside `V₀` or
24	> inside `V₁`.**
25	
26	That is the verdict the lane never obtained.  It is not a statement about pieces, adaptations,
27	tubes or fibres: it says the **assembler route** — every landed producer of `IsCertified` goes
28	through the per-piece no-leak clause — can only ever be driven for divisors confined to one
29	pinned chart of `pi`, a **chart-design** condition.
30	
31	Scope, stated precisely so it is not overread.  What is proved here constrains *leak-freeness*,
32	which is the hypothesis `hnoLeak` of `isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning` and of every
33	assembler downstream of it.  It does **not** yet constrain `IsCertified` itself, because the
34	converse implication
35	
36	  `(∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j))  →  ∀ j, d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅`
37	
38	is **not proved anywhere in this project**: only the three sufficient directions exist
39	(`finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty`, `finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter`,
40	`finite_colength_of_isClopen_trace`).  Its expected proof is that a finite `R`-algebra has a
41	universally closed spectrum, so the locally closed image `supportLocus ∩ pieces j` of
42	`Spec (Γ(pieces j) ⧸ (eqn j))` in the separated `relCurve C R` is closed — real mathlib
43	plumbing, not a corollary.  Until it lands, "`IsCertified` is unsatisfiable off the charts" is a
44	conjecture; "the assembler route is unavailable off the charts" is a theorem.  Roadmap:
45	`…certificate.c1-necessity`.
46	
47	Nor can a shrink of the base repair it, because base localization does not disconnect the
48	divisor: `Spec (R[x]/(x² − t))` over `R = k[t]` is connected over every basic open of
49	`Spec R`, so no Zariski neighbourhood of `t = 0` splits the divisor into clopen packets.
50	Hence the "clopen packet extraction" programme (memory I-0209) is available exactly when the
51	divisor is already chart-confined, and the honest obligation of the lane is to make the
52	DD-R atlas produce chart-confined divisors.
53	
54	## Main declarations
55	
56	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak` —
57	  leak-freeness at a piece plus a connected support forces swallow-or-miss at that piece.
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected` — the
59	  same for every piece at once, i.e. leak-free + connected ⟹ swallow-or-miss.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected` — **the
61	  satisfiability verdict**: a connected support with a leak-free adaptation lies inside one
62	  of the two pinned charts (no nonemptiness needed — the empty support is chart-confined).
63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.not_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isPreconnected` —
64	  the contrapositive obstruction: a connected divisor confined to neither pinned chart admits
65	  no adaptation that is leak-free at every piece.
66	-/
67	
68	set_option autoImplicit false
69	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
70	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161); pin in-file. -/
71	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
72	
73	universe u
74	
75	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
76	
77	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
78	
79	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
80	
81	namespace DivisorAdaptation
82	
83	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
84	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
85	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
86	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
87	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
88	
89	/-! ## Connectedness turns leak-freeness into swallow-or-miss -/
90	
91	/-- **A connected support leaves a leak-free piece no middle ground.** The trace
92	`supportLocus ∩ pieces j` is open in the support because the piece is open, and closed in it
93	because nothing leaks; a preconnected support therefore has the trace empty or total.
94	
95	Stated with `IsPreconnected` on the ambient set (rather than `ConnectedSpace` on the
96	subtype) so that no coercion bookkeeping is needed: the two separating opens are the piece
97	itself and the complement of the — closed — trace. -/
98	theorem subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak (j : A.index)
99	    (hconn : _root_.IsPreconnected d.supportLocus)
100	    (hleak : d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅) :
101	    d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
102	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
103	  classical
104	  have hclosed : IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :=
105	    (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mpr hleak
106	  -- the two separating opens: the piece, and the complement of the (closed) trace
107	  by_cases hdisj : Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
108	  · exact Or.inr hdisj
109	  refine Or.inl ?_
110	  by_contra hnsub
111	  -- both halves are nonempty, so preconnectedness produces a point in their intersection
112	  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := Set.not_disjoint_iff.mp hdisj
113	  obtain ⟨y, hyS, hyU⟩ := Set.not_subset.mp hnsub
114	  obtain ⟨z, hzS, hzu, hzv⟩ :=
115	    hconn (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
116	      (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))ᶜ
117	      (A.pieces j).isOpen hclosed.isOpen_compl
118	      (fun w hw => by
119	        by_cases hwU : w ∈ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
120	        · exact Or.inl hwU
121	        · exact Or.inr fun hc => hwU hc.2)
122	      ⟨x, hx.1, hx.2⟩ ⟨y, hyS, fun hc => hyU hc.2⟩
123	  exact hzv ⟨hzS, hzu⟩
124	
125	/-- **Leak-free at every piece plus a connected support ⟹ swallow-or-miss.** So the
126	hypothesis of `forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` is not an extra assumption for a
127	connected divisor: it is what leak-freeness already says. -/
128	theorem forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected
129	    (hconn : _root_.IsPreconnected d.supportLocus)
130	    (hleak : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅) :
131	    ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
132	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := fun j =>
133	  A.subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak j hconn (hleak j)
134	
135	/-! ## The satisfiability verdict -/
136	
137	/-- **A connected divisor with a leak-free adaptation lies inside one pinned chart.** The
138	verdict the certificate lane needed: the chart-0 dichotomy of `DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean`
139	either puts the support in `V₀` outright, or makes it miss `V₀` entirely — and then
140	`V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤` (`relCover_sup`) puts it in `V₁`.  No nonemptiness is required.
141	
142	Consequently every landed route to `IsCertified` — all of which go through the per-piece
143	no-leak clause — is available for a connected divisor **only** if that divisor avoids
144	`pi⁻¹(∞)` (so it sits in `V₀`) or avoids `pi⁻¹(0)` (so it sits in `V₁`).  This is a
145	condition on the divisor and the chosen `pi`; the adaptation, the support tube, the packet
146	idempotents and the base shrink are all irrelevant to it.  Whether `IsCertified` itself (as
147	opposed to its only known producers) is likewise constrained needs the unproved converse
148	`(c1) → leak-free` discussed in this file's header. -/
149	theorem supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected
150	    (hconn : _root_.IsPreconnected d.supportLocus)
151	    (hleak : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅) :
152	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))
153	      ∨ d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
154	  have hswallow := A.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected hconn hleak
155	  rcases A.subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀ hswallow with h₀ | h₀
156	  · exact Or.inl h₀
157	  -- the support misses `V₀`, so `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤` puts all of it in `V₁`
158	  refine Or.inr fun x hx => ?_
159	  have hmem : x ∈ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
160	      ⊔ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : (relCurve C R).Opens) := by
161	    rw [relCover_sup]; trivial
162	  rcases (Opens.mem_sup ..).mp hmem with h | h
163	  · exact (Set.disjoint_left.mp h₀ hx h).elim
164	  · exact h
165	
166	/-- **The obstruction.** A connected divisor lying in neither pinned chart — i.e. meeting
167	both `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)` — admits **no** adaptation that is leak-free at every piece, over
168	any base and after any shrink; so no landed assembler can certify it.
169	
170	Model to keep in mind: the degree-two relative divisor `V(t x² + x y + t y²) ⊆ ℙ¹` over
171	`k[t]`, whose section ring is a domain (so it is connected over every basic open of
172	`Spec k[t]`) and whose fibre at `t = 0` is `{0, ∞}`. -/
173	theorem not_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isPreconnected
174	    (hconn : _root_.IsPreconnected d.supportLocus)
175	    (h₀ : ¬ d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))
176	    (h₁ : ¬ d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) :
177	    ¬ ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ := fun hleak =>
178	  (A.supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected hconn hleak).elim h₀ h₁

9	/-!
10	# Clause (c1) is *equivalent* to leak-freeness
11	
12	`SupportTubeFinite.lean` proves one direction of the (c1) engine: a closed piece trace makes
13	the chart-local colength a finite `R`-module.  The converse was assumed throughout the
14	certificate lane — memory I-0209 states the Z-clopen principle as an "iff", and
15	`DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean` needs it to upgrade its verdict from "the assembler route is
16	unavailable" to "the certificate itself is unavailable" — but no declaration proved it.
17	
18	It follows from the same triangle the forward direction uses, run backwards.  If
19	`Γ(X, V) ⧸ I` is a finite `R`-module then `Spec (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I) ⟶ Spec R` is a finite morphism,
20	hence universally closed; that morphism factors through `X`, and `X ⟶ Spec R` is separated, so
21	the first leg `Spec (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I) ⟶ X` is universally closed too
22	(`UniversallyClosed.of_comp_of_isSeparated`).  A universally closed morphism is a closed map,
23	so its range — which `range_specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec` identifies with the trace — is closed.
24	
25	Consequences, both recorded here:
26	
27	* the (c1)-finite clause of `IsCertified` is *equivalent* to leak-freeness at that piece, so
28	  the necessity results of `DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` and the verdict of
29	  `DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean` apply to `IsCertified` itself and not only to the assemblers;
30	* in particular a **certified** adaptation of a connected divisor forces that divisor inside a
31	  single pinned chart of `pi`.  `DivFamZar` is therefore blind to connected divisors meeting
32	  both `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)` — over any base, after any Zariski shrink, for any adaptation.
33	
34	## Main declarations
35	
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.isClosed_zeroLocus_inter_of_finite_quotient` — the converse
37	  of the abstract finiteness engine.
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength` — clause
39	  (c1)-finite at a piece implies leak-freeness there.
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLeak_eq_empty_iff_finite_colength` — the two are
41	  equivalent.
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified` — **the
43	  verdict for `IsCertified`**: a certified adaptation of a connected divisor confines it to one
44	  pinned chart.
45	-/

60	/-! ## The converse of the abstract finiteness engine -/
61	
62	namespace IsAffineOpen
63	
64	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
65	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of R))]
66	
67	include hV in
68	/-- **The converse of the abstract (c1) engine.** If the chart-local quotient `Γ(X, V) ⧸ I` is
69	a finite `R`-module then the closed subscheme it cuts has closed image in `X`.
70	
71	The forward direction (`finite_quotient_of_isClosed`) turns closedness into finiteness through
72	`Spec (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I) ⟶ X ⟶ Spec R`; this runs the same triangle backwards.  Finiteness makes
73	the composite universally closed, separatedness of `X ⟶ Spec R` transfers that to the first
74	leg, and a universally closed morphism has closed range. -/
75	theorem isClosed_zeroLocus_inter_of_finite_quotient
76	    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))]
77	    (I : Ideal Γ(X, V)) (h : Module.Finite R (Γ(X, V) ⧸ I)) :
78	    IsClosed (X.zeroLocus (I : Set Γ(X, V)) ∩ (V : Set X)) := by
79	  have hfin : IsFinite ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) ≫ hV.fromSpec)
80	      ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))) := by
81	    rw [Category.assoc, hV.specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec_over]
82	    exact (IsFinite.SpecMap_iff _).mpr (RingHom.finite_algebraMap.mpr h)
83	  haveI : UniversallyClosed (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))
84	      ≫ hV.fromSpec) :=
85	    UniversallyClosed.of_comp_of_isSeparated _ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
86	  rw [← hV.range_specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec I, ← Set.image_univ]
87	  exact (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))
88	    ≫ hV.fromSpec).isClosedMap _ isClosed_univ
89	
90	end IsAffineOpen

92	/-! ## Clause (c1) and leak-freeness are the same condition -/
93	
94	namespace DivisorAdaptation
95	
96	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
97	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
98	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
99	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
100	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
101	
102	/-- **Clause (c1)-finite at a piece implies leak-freeness there** — the direction the lane had
103	assumed since I-0209 without a proof.  With `finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty` it makes
104	the two conditions equivalent. -/
105	theorem supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength (j : A.index)
106	    (h : Module.Finite R (A.colength j)) :
107	    d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ := by
108	  refine (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mp ?_
109	  have hclosed := IsAffineOpen.isClosed_zeroLocus_inter_of_finite_quotient
110	    (A.toFinCoverData.isAffineOpen_pieces j) (Ideal.span {A.eqn j}) h
111	  rw [Scheme.zeroLocus_span] at hclosed
112	  have hset : (relCurve C R).zeroLocus {A.eqn j} ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
113	      = (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
114	        \ ((relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn j) : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
115	    ext x
116	    simp only [Set.mem_inter_iff, Scheme.mem_zeroLocus_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff,
117	      forall_eq, Set.mem_sdiff, SetLike.mem_coe]
118	    exact and_comm
119	  rw [A.supportLocus_inter_pieces j, ← hset]
120	  exact hclosed
121	
122	/-- **Leak-freeness and clause (c1)-finite are the same condition at a piece.** -/
123	theorem supportLeak_eq_empty_iff_finite_colength (j : A.index) :
124	    d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ ↔ Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
125	  ⟨A.finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty j, A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength j⟩
126	
127	/-- **The verdict, for `IsCertified` itself.** A certified adaptation of a connected divisor
128	confines that divisor to a single pinned chart of `pi`.  Together with
129	`DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean`'s obstruction this says `DivFamZar` cannot see a connected divisor
130	meeting both `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)`, over any base and after any Zariski shrink. -/
131	theorem supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified {n : ℕ}
132	    (hconn : _root_.IsPreconnected d.supportLocus) (hc : A.IsCertified n) :
133	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))
134	      ∨ d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
135	  A.supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected hconn
136	    fun j => A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength j (hc.finite_colength j)
137	
138	end DivisorAdaptation

140	end AlgebraicGeometry

10	/-!
11	# The chart-confinement obstruction in witness form
12	
13	`DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean` establishes the verdict positively: a certified adaptation of a
14	connected divisor confines its support to one pinned chart
15	(`supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified`).  Its contrapositive is recorded there only for
16	the *leak-free* hypothesis and only in "not contained in either chart" form.
17	
18	This file states the obstruction in the form a would-be user of the interface meets it: with
19	two **witness points** of the support, one off `V₀` and one off `V₁`.  That is the shape in
20	which a concrete divisor — e.g. one whose fibre over a base point is `{0, ∞}` — refutes
21	certifiability, and it needs no leak hypothesis.
22	
23	Combined with the pullback transport (`DivSchemeCertZarTransport.lean`), which shows support
24	loci pull back along the base-shrinking maps, the obstruction is visibly Zariski-local on the
25	base: shrinking cannot separate the two witnesses.
26	
27	## Main declarations
28	
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses` — a
30	  connected divisor with a support point off each pinned chart admits no certified adaptation,
31	  in any degree.
32	-/
33	
34	set_option autoImplicit false
35	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
36	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161); pin in-file. -/
37	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

39	universe u
40	
41	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
42	
43	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
44	
45	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
46	
47	namespace DivisorAdaptation
48	
49	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
50	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
51	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
52	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
53	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)
54	
55	/-- **The obstruction in witness form.** If the support is connected and contains a point
56	outside `V₀` and a point outside `V₁` — i.e. the divisor genuinely meets both `pi⁻¹(∞)` and
57	`pi⁻¹(0)` — then `A` carries no certificate, in any degree.
58	
59	No leak hypothesis: clause (c1) of `IsCertified` supplies it
60	(`supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength`).  So the interface does not merely make such
61	divisors hard to certify, it excludes them. -/
62	theorem not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses {n : ℕ}
63	    (hconn : _root_.IsPreconnected d.supportLocus)
64	    {x y : relCurve C R} (hx : x ∈ d.supportLocus) (hy : y ∈ d.supportLocus)
65	    (hx₀ : x ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))
66	    (hy₁ : y ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) :
67	    ¬ A.IsCertified n := by
68	  intro hc
69	  rcases A.supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified hconn hc with h₀ | h₁
70	  · exact hx₀ (h₀ hx)
71	  · exact hy₁ (h₁ hy)
72	
73	end DivisorAdaptation
74	
75	end AlgebraicGeometry

7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace
8	
9	/-!
10	# Swallow or miss: the shape of an adaptation that can be certified
11	
12	`DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` shows that the assembler's per-piece no-leak clause
13	*forces* the chart traces `supportLocus ∩ V_b` to be closed.  This file gives the matching
14	sufficient condition, and it is deliberately crude:
15	
16	> if every piece either **swallows** the support (`supportLocus ⊆ pieces j`) or **misses**
17	> it (`Disjoint supportLocus (pieces j)`), then no-leak holds at every piece.
18	
19	For a swallowing piece the trace is the whole support, which is closed by construction
20	(`isClosed_supportLocus`); for a missing piece the trace is empty.  Neither case needs a
21	fibre, a tube, or an idempotent.
22	
23	The crudeness is not a defect, because the necessity lemma pins down exactly how much
24	freedom is left.  Both pinned charts are covered by their pieces, so
25	
26	* if some chart-`b` piece meets the support it must swallow it, whence `supportLocus ⊆ V_b`;
27	* otherwise every chart-`b` piece misses the support, whence `supportLocus ∩ V_b = ∅`.
28	
29	Since `V₀ ⊔ V₁` is the whole relative curve, a nonempty support therefore lies in
30	`V₀ ⊓ V₁` — the divisor must avoid **both** vertical fibres `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)` — or be
31	confined to one of them.  That is the honest chart-design hypothesis of the lane, and it is
32	where the DD-R atlas has to do its work; it is not something a support tube, a packet
33	idempotent, or a shrink of the base can manufacture.
34	
35	A missing piece contributes nothing at all: its equation is a unit, so its colength module
36	vanishes (`subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`) and clauses (c1) hold there for
37	free — no fibrewise regularity input.  So the certificate of a swallow-or-miss adaptation is
38	carried entirely by the swallowing pieces, at most one per chart.
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus` — a
43	  piece missing the support has a vanishing colength.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint` — swallow
45	  or miss gives no-leak at that piece.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` — the
47	  assembler-shaped `hnoLeak`, with no fibre analysis.
48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` —
49	  clause (c1)-finite at every piece.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀` /
51	  `…_chart₁_…` — the design constraint the shape imposes on the divisor.
52	-/
53	
54	set_option autoImplicit false
55	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
56	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161); pin in-file. -/
57	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

59	universe u
60	
61	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
62	
63	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
64	
65	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
66	
67	namespace DivisorAdaptation
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
71	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
72	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
73	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
74	
75	/-! ## A piece missing the support contributes nothing -/
76	
77	/-- **A piece that misses the support has a vanishing colength.** Its equation has a unit
78	germ at every point of the piece (`isUnit_germ_eqn_iff` read through the unit locus), hence
79	is a unit (`RingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ`), hence spans the unit ideal.
80	
81	This is the colength companion of `subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`: on
82	such a piece the certificate's clauses (c1) are free, with no fibrewise regularity input. -/
83	lemma subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus (j : A.index)
84	    (hdisj : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
85	    Subsingleton (A.colength j) := by
86	  have hunit : IsUnit (A.eqn j) := by
87	    apply (relCurve C R).toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
88	    intro z hz
89	    have hU : z ∈ d.unitLocus := not_not.mp (hdisj z hz)
90	    exact (A.isUnit_germ_eqn_iff j hz).mpr
91	      ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens z)).mp hU)
92	  exact Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr
93	    (Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ (Ideal.subset_span rfl) hunit)
94	
95	/-! ## Swallow or miss gives no-leak -/
96	
97	/-- **Swallow or miss gives no-leak at that piece.** If the piece contains the whole support
98	its trace is the support, closed by `isClosed_supportLocus`; if the piece misses the support
99	its trace is empty.  In neither case is a fibre, a tube or an idempotent involved. -/
100	theorem supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint (j : A.index)
101	    (h : d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
102	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
103	    d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ := by
104	  refine (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mp ?_
105	  rcases h with hsub | hdisj
106	  · rw [Set.inter_eq_left.mpr hsub]
107	    exact d.isClosed_supportLocus
108	  · rw [Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp hdisj]
109	    exact isClosed_empty
110	
111	/-- **The assembler-shaped `hnoLeak` from swallow-or-miss.** This is the hypothesis of
112	`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning` /
113	`isCertified_of_noLeak_of_forall_liftQ_injective` /
114	`divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_liftQ_degree`, produced with no fibre analysis. -/
115	theorem forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
116	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
117	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
118	    ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
119	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
120	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
121	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
122	  intro j s x hx
123	  have hleak := A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint j (h j)
124	  by_contra hxU
125	  exact Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp hleak x ⟨hx.2, hxU⟩
126	
127	section Finite
128	
129	/- The finiteness engine consumes the properness licence on the relative curve
130	(`instIsProperRelCurveHom`), so this clause — and only this clause — needs `IsProper`. -/
131	variable [IsProper C.hom]
132	
133	/-- **Clause (c1)-finite at every piece, from swallow-or-miss.** -/
134	theorem forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
135	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
136	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
137	    ∀ j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := fun j =>
138	  A.finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty j
139	    (A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint j (h j))
140	
141	end Finite
142	
143	/-! ## What the shape forces on the divisor
144	
145	The necessity direction of `DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` is sharpened here: because the
146	chart-`b` pieces cover `V_b`, a swallow-or-miss adaptation exists only for a divisor that is
147	either inside a pinned chart or disjoint from it.  Combined with `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤` this says a
148	nonempty support lies in `V₀ ⊓ V₁`, or is confined to one vertical fibre of `pi`.
149	
150	This is the statement the DD-R atlas owes: **the chart's divisors avoid `pi⁻¹(0)` and
151	`pi⁻¹(∞)`.**  It is a hypothesis about the chart, and it is the only remaining geometric
152	input of the (c1) side of the certificate. -/
153	
154	/-- **Chart-0 dichotomy.** A swallow-or-miss adaptation forces the support either inside the
155	pinned chart `V₀` or disjoint from it. -/
156	theorem subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀
157	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
158	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
159	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))
160	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus
161	        ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
162	  by_cases hmeet : ∃ j : Fin A.m₀, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces (Sum.inl j) : Set (relCurve C R))
163	  · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hmeet
164	    exact Or.inl (hj.trans fun x hx => (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₀ j) hx)
165	  · refine Or.inr (Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mpr ?_)
166	    rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₀_eq_iUnion]
167	    refine Set.iUnion_eq_empty.mpr fun j => Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp ?_
168	    exact (h (Sum.inl j)).resolve_left fun hsub => hmeet ⟨j, hsub⟩
169	
170	/-- **Chart-1 dichotomy.** -/
171	theorem subset_chart₁_or_disjoint_chart₁
172	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
173	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
174	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))
175	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus
176	        ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
177	  by_cases hmeet : ∃ j : Fin A.m₁, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces (Sum.inr j) : Set (relCurve C R))
178	  · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hmeet
179	    exact Or.inl (hj.trans fun x hx => (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₁ j) hx)
180	  · refine Or.inr (Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mpr ?_)
181	    rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₁_eq_iUnion]
182	    refine Set.iUnion_eq_empty.mpr fun j => Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp ?_
183	    exact (h (Sum.inr j)).resolve_left fun hsub => hmeet ⟨j, hsub⟩
184	
185	end DivisorAdaptation

9	/-!
10	# The chart trace is what no-leak really asks for
11	
12	The certificate assemblers consume, per piece `j`, the fibrewise no-leak clause, which is
13	emptiness of the leak locus, which is closedness of the piece trace
14	`supportLocus ∩ pieces j` (`isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`), which
15	is clopen-ness of that trace inside the support (`isClopen_trace_of_supportLeak_eq_empty`).
16	
17	This file records the consequence that had been missed for the whole lifetime of the lane:
18	**the per-piece clause cannot be produced piece by piece.**  A `FinCoverData` carries a
19	partition of unity on each pinned chart, so the chart-`b` pieces cover the *whole* pinned
20	chart `V_b` — hence the union of their traces is the whole chart trace
21	`supportLocus ∩ V_b`.  A finite union of closed sets is closed, so
22	
23	> no-leak at every chart-`b` piece **forces** `supportLocus ∩ V_b` to be closed in the
24	> relative curve, i.e. the chart trace to be clopen in the support.
25	
26	That is a property of the *system and the pinned charts alone*: no choice of adaptation, and
27	no shrinking of the base, can produce no-leak for a system whose chart trace is not closed.
28	It is therefore the honest gate of the lane, and it replaces the refuted `tube-fibre`
29	framing (put the support inside one piece — impossible once the support meets both charts,
30	`not_exists_unique_support_piece`) and the refuted separated framing
31	(`DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean`) with a single geometric statement about the divisor.
32	
33	Read positively, it says where to aim, but the converse is **not** the mirror image and this
34	file does not claim it: closed chart traces alone do not produce a leak-free adaptation.  What
35	does is `DivSchemeCertZarChartPair.lean`, and it needs two further inputs — the support inside
36	the chart *overlap* `V₀ ⊓ V₁`, and a chart-principality datum making the two pinned charts
37	themselves legal pieces.  Both are recorded there and on the roadmap
38	(`…certificate.chart-avoid`, `…certificate.swallow-adapt`).
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLocus_inter_chart₀_eq_iUnion` /
43	  `…_chart₁_…` — the chart trace is the finite union of the chart's piece traces.
44	* `DivisorAdaptation.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart₀_of_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty`
45	  and its chart-1 twin — no-leak at every piece of a chart forces the chart trace closed.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak` —
47	  the assembler-shaped form: the `hnoLeak` hypothesis of
48	  `isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning` forces both chart traces closed.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.not_forall_noLeak_of_not_isClosed_chart₀` — the
50	  obstruction, contrapositive: a system with a non-closed chart-0 trace admits **no**
51	  adaptation satisfying the assembler's no-leak clause.
52	-/
53

69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
71	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
72	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
73	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)

75	/-! ## The chart trace is the union of the piece traces -/
76	
77	/-- **The chart-0 trace is the finite union of the chart-0 piece traces.** `⊆` is the
78	partition-of-unity cover `FinCoverData.cover₀`; `⊇` is `Scheme.basicOpen_le`, each piece
79	being a basic open *of* the pinned chart. -/
80	lemma supportLocus_inter_chart₀_eq_iUnion :
81	    d.supportLocus ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))
82	      = ⋃ j : Fin A.m₀, d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces (Sum.inl j) : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
83	  apply Set.eq_of_subset_of_subset
84	  · rintro x ⟨hxs, hxV⟩
85	    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (A.toFinCoverData.cover₀ hxV)
86	    exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨j, hxs, hj⟩
87	  · refine Set.iUnion_subset fun j x hx => ⟨hx.1, ?_⟩
88	    exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₀ j) hx.2
89	
90	/-- **The chart-1 trace is the finite union of the chart-1 piece traces.** -/
91	lemma supportLocus_inter_chart₁_eq_iUnion :
92	    d.supportLocus ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))
93	      = ⋃ j : Fin A.m₁, d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces (Sum.inr j) : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
94	  apply Set.eq_of_subset_of_subset
95	  · rintro x ⟨hxs, hxV⟩
96	    obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (A.toFinCoverData.cover₁ hxV)
97	    exact Set.mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨j, hxs, hj⟩
98	  · refine Set.iUnion_subset fun j x hx => ⟨hx.1, ?_⟩
99	    exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₁ j) hx.2
100	
101	/-! ## No-leak forces the chart trace closed -/
102	
103	/-- **No-leak at every chart-0 piece forces the chart-0 trace closed.** The trace of the
104	whole pinned chart is the finite union of the piece traces, each of which is closed exactly
105	when nothing leaks out of it. -/
106	theorem isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart₀_of_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty
107	    (h : ∀ j : Fin A.m₀, d.supportLeak (A.pieces (Sum.inl j)) = ∅) :
108	    IsClosed (d.supportLocus
109	      ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))) := by
110	  rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₀_eq_iUnion]
111	  exact isClosed_iUnion_of_finite fun j =>
112	    (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty _).mpr (h j)
113	
114	/-- **No-leak at every chart-1 piece forces the chart-1 trace closed.** -/
115	theorem isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart₁_of_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty
116	    (h : ∀ j : Fin A.m₁, d.supportLeak (A.pieces (Sum.inr j)) = ∅) :
117	    IsClosed (d.supportLocus
118	      ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) := by
119	  rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₁_eq_iUnion]
120	  exact isClosed_iUnion_of_finite fun j =>
121	    (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty _).mpr (h j)
122	
123	/-- **The assembler's `hnoLeak` hypothesis forces both chart traces closed.** This is the
124	gate of the certificate lane in its irreducible form: the hypothesis of
125	`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning` (equivalently of
126	`isCertified_of_noLeak_of_forall_liftQ_injective`,
127	`divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_liftQ_degree`) implies a statement that mentions
128	neither the adaptation nor its pieces — only the system and the two pinned charts. -/
129	theorem isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak
130	    (hnoLeak : ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
131	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
132	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
133	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
134	    IsClosed (d.supportLocus
135	        ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))
136	      ∧ IsClosed (d.supportLocus
137	        ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) := by
138	  have hleak : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅ := fun j =>
139	    d.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_forall_fibre
140	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) (hnoLeak j)
141	  exact ⟨A.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart₀_of_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty
142	      fun j => hleak (Sum.inl j),
143	    A.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart₁_of_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty
144	      fun j => hleak (Sum.inr j)⟩
145	
146	/-! ## The obstruction
147	
148	The contrapositive is the statement the lane needed: for a system whose chart trace is not
149	closed there is *nothing to prove* — the assembler's hypothesis is false for every
150	adaptation, so no support-tube refinement, no idempotent packet extraction and no shrinking
151	of the base can supply it.  The tube mechanism (`exists_basicOpen_supportLeak_eq_empty`)
152	is not a counterexample: it shrinks the base, and shrinking the base shrinks the system's
153	support too, so what it proves is the chart-trace statement over the smaller base. -/
154	
155	/-- **The obstruction.** If the chart-0 trace of the system is not closed in the relative
156	curve, then no adaptation of that system satisfies the assembler's no-leak clause. -/
157	theorem not_forall_noLeak_of_not_isClosed_chart₀
158	    (hnc : ¬ IsClosed (d.supportLocus
159	      ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))) :
160	    ¬ ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
161	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
162	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
163	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
164	  fun h => hnc (A.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak h).1
165	
166	/-- **The obstruction, chart 1.** -/
167	theorem not_forall_noLeak_of_not_isClosed_chart₁
168	    (hnc : ¬ IsClosed (d.supportLocus
169	      ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)))) :
170	    ¬ ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
171	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
172	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
173	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
174	  fun h => hnc (A.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak h).2
175	
176	end DivisorAdaptation

9	/-!
10	# The coarse adaptation: one piece per pinned chart
11	
12	`DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean` decides which divisors the assembler route can reach at all: a
13	connected one must lie inside a single pinned chart.  This file supplies the adaptation to use
14	once that holds, and it is the coarsest one possible — **one piece per chart, the chart
15	itself**.
16	
17	`FinCoverData` asks for a partition of unity on each pinned chart; taking a single generator
18	`h = 1` with coefficient `a = 1` satisfies it trivially, and `Scheme.basicOpen_one` identifies
19	the resulting piece with the chart.  Feeding that cover data to the landed anchored
20	constructor `DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors` turns a *chart-principality* datum — one member of
21	`d`'s cover containing each pinned chart, with a comparison unit — into an adaptation whose
22	two pieces are `V₀` and `V₁`.
23	
24	For that adaptation the certificate's per-piece obligations are as small as they can be:
25	
26	* if `supportLocus ⊆ V₀ ⊓ V₁` then **both** pieces swallow the support, so `hnoLeak` and
27	  clause (c1)-finite hold at every piece (`DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean`), with no fibre
28	  analysis and no packet idempotent;
29	* none of the landed no-gos touches this configuration.  `not_exists_unique_support_piece`
30	  refutes *one* support-meeting piece and this adaptation has *two*;
31	  `supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated` refutes *separation* and this adaptation is
32	  as unseparated as possible — its two pieces share the whole overlap.
33	
34	The residual hypothesis, chart principality, is the honest one: it says the divisor is cut by
35	a single equation on each pinned chart, i.e. it is the statement that the DD-R window's local
36	generators can be taken globally on a chart.  The pointwise gate
37	(`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation`) licenses shrinking the base
38	before asking for it.
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartPairCoverData` — the two-piece cover data, one piece per pinned
43	  chart, with `pieces_inl`/`pieces_inr` identifying the pieces with `V₀` and `V₁`.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.ofChartPair` — the adaptation from a chart-principality
45	  datum.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.ofChartPair_pieces_eq_chart` — its pieces are the
47	  pinned charts.
48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_pieces_eq_chart` — a
49	  divisor inside the chart overlap is swallowed by every chart-shaped piece.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_pieces_eq_chart` and
51	  `forall_finite_colength_of_pieces_eq_chart` — the assembler's `hnoLeak` and clause
52	  (c1)-finite for a chart-shaped adaptation of a chart-overlap divisor.
53	-/
54

72	/-! ## The coarse cover data -/
73	
74	/-- **The two-piece cover data**: one piece per pinned chart, generated by `1`.  The partition
75	of unity is `1 * 1 = 1` over `Fin 1`, so no geometry is consumed. -/
76	noncomputable def chartPairCoverData : FinCoverData C R π where
77	  m₀ := 1
78	  m₁ := 1
79	  h₀ := fun _ => 1
80	  h₁ := fun _ => 1
81	  a₀ := fun _ => 1
82	  a₁ := fun _ => 1
83	  partition₀ := by simp
84	  partition₁ := by simp
85	
86	@[simp]
87	lemma chartPairCoverData_pieces_inl (j : Fin (chartPairCoverData C R π).m₀) :
88	    (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces (Sum.inl j)
89	      = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ := by
90	  rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inl]
91	  exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_one
92	
93	@[simp]
94	lemma chartPairCoverData_pieces_inr (j : Fin (chartPairCoverData C R π).m₁) :
95	    (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces (Sum.inr j)
96	      = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := by
97	  rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inr]
98	  exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_one
99	
100	/-- Every piece of the coarse cover data is one of the two pinned charts. -/
101	lemma chartPairCoverData_pieces_eq (j : (chartPairCoverData C R π).index) :
102	    (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
103	      ∨ (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := by
104	  cases j with
105	  | inl j => exact Or.inl (chartPairCoverData_pieces_inl C R π j)
106	  | inr j => exact Or.inr (chartPairCoverData_pieces_inr C R π j)
107	
108	namespace DivisorAdaptation
109	
110	variable {C R π} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
111	
112	/-- **The coarse adaptation from a chart-principality datum.** `pt` names, for each pinned
113	chart, a member of `d`'s cover containing that whole chart; `eqn` is the chart equation and
114	`unit` the comparison unit against `d`'s equation there.  The result is an adaptation whose
115	two pieces are the pinned charts themselves. -/
116	noncomputable def ofChartPair
117	    (eqn : ∀ j : (chartPairCoverData C R π).index,
118	      Γ(relCurve C R, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j))
119	    (pt : (chartPairCoverData C R π).index → relCurve C R)
120	    (piece_le : ∀ j, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
121	    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j)ˣ)
122	    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j
123	      = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j))
124	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
125	    DivisorAdaptation C R π d :=
126	  DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors (chartPairCoverData C R π) eqn pt piece_le unit eqn_eq
127	
128	/-- **The pieces of `ofChartPair` are the pinned charts.** The anchored constructor keeps the
129	supplied cover data, so this is definitional plus `Scheme.basicOpen_one`. -/
130	lemma ofChartPair_pieces_eq_chart
131	    (eqn : ∀ j : (chartPairCoverData C R π).index,
132	      Γ(relCurve C R, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j))
133	    (pt : (chartPairCoverData C R π).index → relCurve C R)
134	    (piece_le : ∀ j, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
135	    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j)ˣ)
136	    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j
137	      = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j))
138	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)))
139	    (j : (ofChartPair eqn pt piece_le unit eqn_eq).index) :
140	    (ofChartPair eqn pt piece_le unit eqn_eq).pieces j
141	        = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
142	      ∨ (ofChartPair eqn pt piece_le unit eqn_eq).pieces j
143	        = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ :=
144	  chartPairCoverData_pieces_eq C R π j
145	
146	/-! ## The certificate obligations for a chart-shaped adaptation
147	
148	Stated against the *shape* of the pieces rather than against `ofChartPair` itself, so that any
149	adaptation whose pieces are the two pinned charts — however it was built — qualifies. -/
150	
151	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
152	
153	/-- **A divisor inside the chart overlap is swallowed by every chart-shaped piece.** -/
154	theorem forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_pieces_eq_chart
155	    (hpieces : ∀ j : A.index, A.pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
156	      ∨ A.pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
157	    (hsub : d.supportLocus ⊆ (((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
158	      ⊓ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : (relCurve C R).Opens) : Set (relCurve C R))) :
159	    ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
160	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
161	  intro j
162	  refine Or.inl fun x hx => ?_
163	  have hx' := hsub hx
164	  rcases hpieces j with h | h <;> rw [h]
165	  · exact hx'.1
166	  · exact hx'.2
167	
168	/-- **The assembler's `hnoLeak` for a chart-shaped adaptation of a chart-overlap divisor.** No
169	fibre, no tube, no packet idempotent. -/
170	theorem forall_noLeak_of_pieces_eq_chart
171	    (hpieces : ∀ j : A.index, A.pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
172	      ∨ A.pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
173	    (hsub : d.supportLocus ⊆ (((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
174	      ⊓ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : (relCurve C R).Opens) : Set (relCurve C R))) :
175	    ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
176	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
177	          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
178	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
179	  A.forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
180	    (A.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_pieces_eq_chart hpieces hsub)

182	section Finite

184	variable [IsProper C.hom]
185	
186	/-- **Clause (c1)-finite for a chart-shaped adaptation of a chart-overlap divisor.** -/
187	theorem forall_finite_colength_of_pieces_eq_chart
188	    (hpieces : ∀ j : A.index, A.pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
189	      ∨ A.pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
190	    (hsub : d.supportLocus ⊆ (((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
191	      ⊓ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : (relCurve C R).Opens) : Set (relCurve C R))) :
192	    ∀ j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
193	  A.forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
194	    (A.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_pieces_eq_chart hpieces hsub)

9	/-!
10	# Chart confinement: a divisor invariant, and an open condition on the base
11	
12	`DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean` proves the negative half of the certificate lane's gate: a certified
13	adaptation of a connected divisor confines that divisor to one pinned chart of `π`
14	(`supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified`).  This file supplies the two facts that turn that
15	no-go into a *decision* about the interface rather than an open question.
16	
17	**1. The obstruction is about the divisor, not the presentation.**  `DivFamZar` is a `DivEq`
18	quotient, so a no-go stated about a local-equation system only bites the functor if it is
19	`DivEq`-invariant.  `DivEq.supportLocus_eq` proves it is: the unit locus is defined by germ
20	invertibility, and `DivEq` changes germs by units.  Hence
21	`not_isCertified_of_divEq_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses`: no representative of the divisor
22	class admits a certified adaptation.  Re-spelling the equations cannot escape the obstruction.
23	
24	**2. Confinement is an OPEN condition on the base.**  The support is closed and the relative
25	curve is proper over the test ring, so the set of base points whose support fibre lies in the
26	chart overlap `V₀ ⊓ V₁` is open (`isOpen_setOf_fibre_subset_chartInter`), and confinement at a
27	single fibre spreads to a Zariski neighbourhood
28	(`exists_opens_supportLocus_subset_chartInter`, the chart instance of the landed support tube).
29	
30	Fact 2 is the licence the lane needs.  `IsLocallyCertified` — hence `DivFamZar` — is a
31	Zariski-local-on-the-base condition, and an *open* condition on the base may legitimately be
32	imposed by an atlas: the charts still cover.  So the repair of the interface is not "assume the
33	divisor avoids the vertical fibres" (a hypothesis on an arbitrary divisor, which
34	`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §Discipline (2) rightly forbids) but "the chart of the atlas records
35	which vertical fibres its divisors avoid" — legitimate exactly because the recorded condition
36	is open.  What Fact 2 does *not* supply, and what the repair still owes, is that these opens
37	COVER: with the two pinned charts fixed once and for all they provably do not
38	(`not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses` applies to a connected divisor meeting both
39	vertical fibres over a base point, and no Zariski shrink separates the witnesses).
40	
41	Finally `supportLocus_subset_of_forall_fibre` converts the global confinement hypothesis of
42	`forall_finite_colength_of_pieces_eq_chart` into the fibrewise one the seed geometry actually
43	produces, so the chart-shaped adaptation's clause (c1) can be discharged fibre by fibre.
44	
45	## Main declarations
46	
47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq.unitLocus_eq` /
48	  `DivEq.supportLocus_eq` — the unit locus and the support locus are divisor invariants.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_isCertified` /
50	  `not_isCertified_of_not_isClosed_inter_chart₀` — the obstruction with NO connectivity
51	  hypothesis: a certificate forces both chart traces closed.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.not_isCertified_of_divEq_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses`
53	  — the obstruction descends to the `DivEq` quotient the functor is built from.
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_opens_supportLocus_subset_chartInter` —
55	  fibrewise chart confinement spreads to a Zariski neighbourhood of the base point.
56	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.isOpen_setOf_fibre_subset_chartInter` — the
57	  confinement locus of the base is open.
58	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.supportLocus_subset_of_forall_fibre` — fibrewise
59	  confinement at every base point is global confinement.
60	-/

77	/-! ## The support locus is a divisor invariant -/
78	
79	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
80	
81	/-- **The unit locus only depends on the divisor.**  Two `DivEq` systems have equations that
82	agree up to a unit on a common refinement, and the unit locus is a germ-invertibility locus, so
83	it cannot see the unit. -/
84	theorem DivEq.unitLocus_eq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) :
85	    (d₁.unitLocus : Set X) = (d₂.unitLocus : Set X) := by
86	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
87	  ext y
88	  have hyW : y ∈ 𝒲.opens y := 𝒲.mem_opens y
89	  have hy₁ : y ∈ d₁.cover.opens y := h₁ y hyW
90	  have hy₂ : y ∈ d₂.cover.opens y := h₂ y hyW
91	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H y
92	  have key := congrArg (X.presheaf.germ (𝒲.opens y) y hyW).hom hu
93	  rw [map_mul] at key
94	  rw [show (X.presheaf.germ (𝒲.opens y) y hyW).hom
95	      ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁ y)).op).hom (d₁.eqn y))
96	      = (X.presheaf.germ (d₁.cover.opens y) y hy₁).hom (d₁.eqn y) from
97	    TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply _ _ _ _ _] at key
98	  rw [show (X.presheaf.germ (𝒲.opens y) y hyW).hom
99	      ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₂ y)).op).hom (d₂.eqn y))
100	      = (X.presheaf.germ (d₂.cover.opens y) y hy₂).hom (d₂.eqn y) from
101	    TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply _ _ _ _ _] at key
102	  simp only [SetLike.mem_coe]
103	  rw [d₁.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hy₁, d₂.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hy₂, key,
104	    IsUnit.mul_iff]
105	  exact and_iff_right (u.isUnit.map _)
106	
107	/-- **The support locus only depends on the divisor** — the complement of
108	`DivEq.unitLocus_eq`.  This is what makes every no-go about `supportLocus` a statement about
109	the `DivFam`/`DivFamZar` quotient and not merely about a chosen representative. -/
110	theorem DivEq.supportLocus_eq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) :
111	    d₁.supportLocus = d₂.supportLocus := by
112	  rw [supportLocus, supportLocus, h.unitLocus_eq]

114	/-! ## Fibrewise confinement, and its base-open spread -/
115	
116	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
117	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
118	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
119	
120	omit [IsProper C.hom] in
121	/-- **Fibrewise confinement at every base point is global confinement**: the fibres of the
122	structure morphism cover the relative curve.  This is the form in which the chart-shaped
123	adaptation's clause (c1) hypothesis
124	(`DivisorAdaptation.forall_finite_colength_of_pieces_eq_chart`) meets the fibrewise geometry
125	the seed actually produces. -/
126	theorem supportLocus_subset_of_forall_fibre (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
127	    (U : (relCurve C R).Opens)
128	    (h : ∀ s : Spec (.of R), ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆
129	      (U : Set (relCurve C R))) :
130	    d.supportLocus ⊆ (U : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
131	  fun _ hx => h _ ⟨rfl, hx⟩
132	
133	/-- **Chart confinement spreads from one fibre to a Zariski neighbourhood of the base.**  The
134	chart instance of the landed support tube (`exists_supportTube`), at the chart overlap
135	`V₀ ⊓ V₁` — the open in which a chart-shaped adaptation swallows the divisor. -/
136	theorem exists_opens_supportLocus_subset_chartInter (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
137	    (s : Spec (.of R))
138	    (hfib : ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆
139	      (((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ :
140	        (relCurve C R).Opens) : Set (relCurve C R))) :
141	    ∃ V : (Spec (.of R)).Opens, s ∈ V ∧
142	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' (V : Set (Spec (.of R))) ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆
143	        (((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ :
144	          (relCurve C R).Opens) : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
145	  d.exists_supportTube ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)) (Opens.isOpen _) hfib
146	
147	/-- **Chart confinement is an OPEN condition on the base.**  The base points over which the
148	divisor is confined to the chart overlap form an open subset of `Spec R`.
149	
150	This is the licence for an atlas to record chart avoidance: an open condition may be imposed
151	chart-wise without losing points, whereas a closed or arbitrary one may not.  It does not by
152	itself say the resulting opens cover — with the two pinned charts fixed they provably do not,
153	by `DivisorAdaptation.not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses`. -/
154	theorem isOpen_setOf_fibre_subset_chartInter (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
155	    IsOpen {s : Spec (.of R) |
156	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆
157	        (((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ :
158	          (relCurve C R).Opens) : Set (relCurve C R))} := by
159	  rw [isOpen_iff_forall_mem_open]
160	  intro s hs
161	  obtain ⟨V, hsV, hV⟩ := exists_opens_supportLocus_subset_chartInter d s hs
162	  refine ⟨(V : Set (Spec (.of R))), ?_, V.isOpen, hsV⟩
163	  intro s' hs' x hx
164	  refine hV ⟨?_, hx.2⟩
165	  have hxs : ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base x = s' := hx.1
166	  rw [Set.mem_preimage, hxs]
167	  exact hs'
168	
169	end Scheme.LocalEquations

171	/-! ## The obstruction descends to the divisor class -/
172	
173	namespace DivisorAdaptation
174	
175	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
176	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
177	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
178	
179	/-- **The chart obstruction in its strongest form: no connectivity hypothesis at all.**  A
180	certified adaptation forces BOTH pinned-chart traces of the support to be closed in the relative
181	curve — a statement in which neither the adaptation nor its pieces nor any connectivity
182	assumption appears.
183	
184	This is the honest shape of the design failure.  `supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified`
185	derives the chart *containment* from it, but needs the support preconnected; the closedness
186	itself does not, and already refutes certifiability for any divisor whose chart trace is dense
187	and not closed — for instance the degree-two divisor `V(t·x² + x·y + t·y²)` over `k[t]`, whose
188	fibre at `t = 0` is `{0, ∞}` (the model recorded at
189	`DivSchemeCertZarConn.not_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isPreconnected`), where
190	`supportLocus ∩ V₀` is the irreducible support minus one point. -/
191	theorem isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_isCertified {n : ℕ}
192	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d) (hc : A.IsCertified n) :
193	    IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))) ∧
194	      IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) :=
195	  ⟨A.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart₀_of_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty fun j =>
196	      A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength _ (hc.finite_colength (Sum.inl j)),
197	    A.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart₁_of_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty fun j =>
198	      A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_finite_colength _ (hc.finite_colength (Sum.inr j))⟩
199	
200	/-- **The obstruction with no connectivity hypothesis, in refuting form.**  A divisor one of
201	whose pinned-chart traces fails to be closed admits no certified adaptation, in any degree. -/
202	theorem not_isCertified_of_not_isClosed_inter_chart₀ {n : ℕ}
203	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
204	    (h : ¬ IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩
205	      ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))) :
206	    ¬ A.IsCertified n :=
207	  fun hc => h (A.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_isCertified hc).1
208	
209	/-- **The chart obstruction is a statement about the divisor class.**  If *some* representative
210	`d₁` of the class has connected support with a point off `V₀` and a point off `V₁`, then *no*
211	representative `d₂` of the same class admits a certified adaptation.
212	
213	`DivFamZar` is a `DivEq` quotient, so this — not the representative-level statement — is what
214	tells the functor apart from the relative-divisor functor. -/
215	theorem not_isCertified_of_divEq_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses {n : ℕ}
216	    {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (h : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁ d₂)
217	    (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d₂)
218	    (hconn : _root_.IsPreconnected d₁.supportLocus)
219	    {x y : relCurve C R} (hx : x ∈ d₁.supportLocus) (hy : y ∈ d₁.supportLocus)
220	    (hx₀ : x ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)))
221	    (hy₁ : y ∉ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))) :
222	    ¬ A.IsCertified n := by
223	  rw [h.supportLocus_eq] at hconn hx hy
224	  exact A.not_isCertified_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses hconn hx hy hx₀ hy₁
225	
226	end DivisorAdaptation

9	/-!
10	# From pointwise away-certificates to a span-`⊤` family
11	
12	`DivSchemeCertZarSeed.lean` reduced the DD-R certificate gate to *away-local* certificates
13	over a span-`⊤` family.  The geometry that produces such certificates, however, is
14	pointwise on the base: the support tube (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`)
15	isolates the pieces over a Zariski neighbourhood **of one base point at a time**, and the
16	fibre analyses all read at a single `p : PrimeSpectrum R`.
17	
18	This file closes that gap with the quasi-compactness step.  If for every prime `p` there
19	is some `r ∉ p` over whose away localization the system is certified, then the good
20	elements span the unit ideal (their basic opens cover `Spec R`), so finitely many of them
21	already do — and `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` applies.
22	
23	The result is that the certificate gate for the DD-R endgame is now genuinely *pointwise*:
24	one base point at a time, exactly the shape the landed fibre machinery delivers.
25	
26	## Main declarations
27	
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away` — the pointwise gate
29	  for a bare local-equation system.
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified`
31	  — the seed form.
32	-/
33	
34	set_option autoImplicit false
35	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
36	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

46	/-! ## The quasi-compactness step -/
47	
48	section SpanTop
49	
50	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
51	
52	/-- **Pointwise good elements span the unit ideal, finitely.** If a predicate `P` on `R`
53	holds at some element outside each prime, then finitely many elements satisfying `P` span
54	`⊤`.  This is quasi-compactness of `Spec R` in the elementary form the certificate gate
55	needs: the basic opens of the good elements cover the spectrum, hence the good set spans
56	the unit ideal, hence `1` is a finite combination of good elements. -/
57	theorem exists_fin_span_eq_top_of_forall_prime (P : R → Prop)
58	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ P r) :
59	    ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, P (g i) := by
60	  classical
61	  -- the good elements span the unit ideal, because their basic opens cover `Spec R`
62	  have hspan : Ideal.span {r : R | P r} = ⊤ := by
63	    rw [← PrimeSpectrum.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff']
64	    refine top_le_iff.mp fun p _ => ?_
65	    obtain ⟨r, hrp, hrP⟩ := h p
66	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨r, by
67	      simpa only [Opens.mem_iSup, PrimeSpectrum.mem_basicOpen] using ⟨hrP, hrp⟩⟩
68	  -- `1` is then a finite combination of good elements
69	  have hone : (1 : R) ∈ Submodule.span R {r : R | P r} := by
70	    show (1 : R) ∈ Ideal.span {r : R | P r}
71	    rw [hspan]; exact Submodule.mem_top
72	  obtain ⟨T, hTsub, hT⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_finite_of_mem_span hone
73	  refine ⟨T.card, fun i => (T.equivFin.symm i : R), ?_, fun i => hTsub (T.equivFin.symm i).2⟩
74	  have hrange : Set.range (fun i : Fin T.card => ((T.equivFin.symm i : R))) = (T : Set R) := by
75	    ext x
76	    constructor
77	    · rintro ⟨i, rfl⟩
78	      exact (T.equivFin.symm i).2
79	    · intro hx
80	      exact ⟨T.equivFin ⟨x, hx⟩, by simp⟩
81	  rw [hrange]
82	  exact Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ hT isUnit_one
83	
84	end SpanTop

86	/-! ## The pointwise certificate gate -/
87	
88	section Pointwise
89	
90	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
91	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
92	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
93	
94	/-- **The pointwise certificate gate.** If over every prime of the base there is an away
95	localization carrying a certified family divisor-equal to the pulled system, the system is
96	locally certified.  Combines the quasi-compactness step with the span-`⊤` production rule
97	`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away`. -/
98	theorem isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away {n : ℕ}
99	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
100	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
101	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
102	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
103	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away r) pi n,
104	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
105	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
106	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
107	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))) :
108	    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n d := by
109	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hgood⟩ := exists_fin_span_eq_top_of_forall_prime
110	    (fun r =>
111	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
112	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
113	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away r) pi n,
114	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
115	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
116	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
117	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) d))) h
118	  exact isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away g hg hgood
119	
120	end Pointwise

122	namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed
123	
124	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
125	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
126	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
127	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
128	variable {a n : ℕ} {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R pi a)}
129	variable {D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R pi a K}
130	
131	omit [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
132	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
133	
134	/-- **The pointwise certificate gate for a seed.** One base point at a time: an away
135	localization at each prime carrying a certified family divisor-equal to the pulled seed
136	system makes the seed's system locally certified, hence a `DivFamZar` class.
137	
138	This is the shape the landed geometry actually produces — the support tube isolates pieces
139	over a neighbourhood of one base point, and every fibre analysis reads at a single prime —
140	so no globally valid no-leak hypothesis (false in general, I-0209) is required anywhere. -/
141	theorem isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified (hD : D.IsGenerator)
142	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
143	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
144	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
145	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away r) pi n,
146	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
147	          ((D.localEquations hD).pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
148	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
149	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) (D.localEquations hD)))) :
150	    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n (D.localEquations hD) :=
151	  isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away h
152	
153	/-- **The gate in its most consumable form: certify the pulled system after shrinking.**
154	At every prime it suffices to produce an `r ∉ p` and a certificate for *some* adaptation
155	of the pulled seed system over `Localization.Away r`.  The adaptation itself is free
156	(`exists_divisorAdaptation`), so the only genuine obligation is the certificate over the
157	shrunken base — where the support tube makes per-piece isolation available.
158	
159	Contrast with the old gate `divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`,
160	which demanded a certificate for the *canonically extracted* adaptation over the whole
161	chart ring; that shape forces a globally valid no-leak hypothesis, which is false. -/
162	theorem isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation
163	    (hD : D.IsGenerator)
164	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
165	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
166	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
167	      ∃ A : DivisorAdaptation C (Localization.Away r) pi
168	          ((D.localEquations hD).pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
169	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
170	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) (D.localEquations hD))),
171	        A.IsCertified n) :
172	    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n (D.localEquations hD) := by
173	  refine isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified hD fun p => ?_
174	  obtain ⟨r, hrp, A, hA⟩ := h p
175	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
176	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
177	  -- bundle the supplied adaptation and its certificate; the divisor equality is `rfl`
178	  exact ⟨r, hrp, ⟨_, A, hA⟩, Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _⟩
179	
180	/-- The `DivFamZar` class of a seed certified pointwise on the base. -/
181	noncomputable def divFamZar_of_forall_prime_away_certified (hD : D.IsGenerator)
182	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
183	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) :=
184	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away r) r
185	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away r) pi n,
186	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
187	          ((D.localEquations hD).pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))
188	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
189	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r)) (D.localEquations hD)))) :
190	    DivFamZar C R pi n :=
191	  DivFamZar.mk (D.localEquations hD)
192	    (isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified hD h)

12	
13	The certificate assemblers take a submodule `L ≤ ker (δ_left − δ_right)` together with the
14	fibrewise-spanning law `hspan`.  Choosing `L` is not where the difficulty lies: the
15	canonical choice `L = ker (δ_left − δ_right)` always satisfies `hle` by `le_rfl`, and for
16	that choice `hspan` is *equivalent* to residue-fibre injectivity of the injectivized map
17	(`ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_iff_liftQ_rTensor_injective`).

20	It is a packaging step, not a weakening: the remaining content is the fibre injectivity,
21	which the syzygy file already shows is equivalent to the flat-cokernel clause and so
22	genuinely needs relative geometry (it is not evadable by a cleverer choice of `L`).
23

25	is now exactly two fibrewise facts: support containment in a piece, and injectivity of the
26	injectivized Čech difference on each residue fibre.

30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_noLeak_of_forall_liftQ_injective` —

69	      (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :

72	          (Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField))

74	    (hovlFlat : Module.Flat R A.ovlProd)
75	    (hinj : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,

10	/-!
11	# Zariski-local certification of a seed system: relaxing the global certificate gate
12	
13	The DD-R endgame consumes divisor families through `DivFamZar` (`DivisorFamilyZar.lean`),
14	whose membership predicate is `IsLocallyCertified`: some span-`⊤` family `g : Fin m → R`
15	carries certified families over the localizations `Localization.Away (g i)` which are
16	divisor-equal to the pulled system.  **Nothing downstream of `DivFamZar` asks for a
17	certificate over `R` itself.**
18	
19	The certificate-assembly lane has nevertheless been attacking the *global* clause
20	`(D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g` over the chart ring `R_Z`, whose no-leak input
21	is exactly the hypothesis that is FALSE for arbitrary extracted pieces (I-0209: a piece
22	whose support trace leaks has a non-finite colength, and the localization repair breaks
23	finiteness over `R`).  The lane has been paying for a strictly stronger statement than
24	its consumer needs.
25	
26	This file lands the relaxation.  `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` says: to
27	certify a system *Zariski-locally* it suffices to produce, for each member of some
28	span-`⊤` family, a certified family over that localization which is divisor-equal to the
29	pulled system.  Then `ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_away_isCertified`
30	specializes it to a seed: if the seed's adaptation acquires a certificate **after
31	localizing at each member of a span-`⊤` family** — which is precisely what the support
32	tube produces (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`: piece isolation is available
33	Zariski-locally on the base, never globally) — then the seed's own system is locally
34	certified, and hence has a `DivFamZar` class.
35	
36	The mathematical content is the observation that `IsLocallyCertified` is designed to be
37	produced from local data and that the seed's pulled system over an away localization is
38	`DivEq` to the pulled adaptation's system on the nose; the localization step that makes
39	no-leak true is licensed here rather than being an unrecoverable obstruction.
40	
41	## Main declarations
42	
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` — the span-`⊤` production
44	  rule for `IsLocallyCertified`, stated with `Localization.Away` charts.
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_away_certified` —
46	  the seed form: away-local certificates give a locally certified seed system.
47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.divFamZar_of_forall_away_certified` — the
48	  resulting `DivFamZar` class, the object every DD-R consumer actually wants.
49	-/
50	
51	set_option autoImplicit false
52	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
53	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161); pin in-file. -/
54	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

58	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
