60	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
61	
62	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
63	
64	section Zariski
65	
66	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
67	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
68	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
69	
70	/-- **The span-`⊤` production rule for local certification.** A local-equation system on
71	the relative curve is locally certified in degree `n` as soon as, over each member of
72	some span-`⊤` family of the base, a certified family is divisor-equal to the pulled
73	system.  This is definitionally `IsLocallyCertified`, exposed as a constructor so that
74	consumers never unfold the pin — and so that the *localization* step (the only place
75	where per-piece support isolation is available, `exists_supportTube`) is a licensed
76	input rather than an obstruction. -/
77	theorem isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away {n m : ℕ} (g : Fin m → R)
78	    (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
79	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
80	    (hcert : ∀ i : Fin m,
81	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
82	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
83	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (g i)) pi n,
84	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
85	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
86	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
87	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) d))) :
88	    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n d :=
89	  ⟨m, g, hg, hcert⟩
90	
91	end Zariski

93	namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed
94	
95	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
96	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
97	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
98	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
99	variable {a n : ℕ} {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R pi a)}
100	variable {D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R pi a K}
101	
102	/- The curve instances are carried by the seed's own data; none of the declarations
103	below re-derives geometry from them. -/
104	omit [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
105	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
106	
107	/-- **Away-local certificates give a locally certified seed system.** If over each member
108	of a span-`⊤` family the seed's pulled system is divisor-equal to a certified family, the
109	seed's own local-equation system is locally certified in degree `n`.
110	
111	This is the honest replacement for the global certificate gate: the seed's no-leak input
112	is false for arbitrary extracted pieces (I-0209), but becomes available after shrinking
113	the base, and `DivFamZar` — the actual DD-R consumer — only ever needs the shrunken
114	data. -/
115	theorem isLocallyCertified_of_forall_away_certified (hD : D.IsGenerator)
116	    {m : ℕ} (g : Fin m → R) (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
117	    (hcert : ∀ i : Fin m,
118	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
119	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
120	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (g i)) pi n,
121	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
122	          ((D.localEquations hD).pullback
123	            (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
124	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
125	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) (D.localEquations hD)))) :
126	    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n (D.localEquations hD) :=
127	  isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away g hg hcert
128	
129	/-- **The `DivFamZar` class of a Zariski-locally certified seed** — the object every DD-R
130	consumer (`divRepPullAt`, `DivRepAffinePullback.pull`, `divRepClassifyZar`) actually
131	takes as input.  No global `IsCertified` over `R` is required. -/
132	noncomputable def divFamZar_of_forall_away_certified (hD : D.IsGenerator)
133	    {m : ℕ} (g : Fin m → R) (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
134	    (hcert : ∀ i : Fin m,
135	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
136	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
137	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (Localization.Away (g i)) pi n,
138	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
139	          ((D.localEquations hD).pullback
140	            (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
141	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
142	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) (D.localEquations hD)))) :
143	    DivFamZar C R pi n :=
144	  DivFamZar.mk (D.localEquations hD)
145	    (isLocallyCertified_of_forall_away_certified hD g hg hcert)
146	
147	/-- The global certificate still suffices, through the trivial one-member family: a
148	globally certified seed is locally certified.  Recorded so that the relaxation is a
149	genuine weakening of the old gate rather than a parallel track. -/
150	theorem isLocallyCertified_of_isCertified (hD : D.IsGenerator)
151	    (hc : (D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified n) :
152	    IsLocallyCertified C R pi n (D.localEquations hD) := by
153	  have h := (D.certifiedFamily n hD hc).isLocallyCertified
154	  rwa [D.certifiedFamily_eqns hD hc] at h
155	
156	end ThetaGeneratorSeed

158	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# The support of a pulled-back system is the preimage of the support
11	
12	The pointwise certificate gate (`DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean`) asks, at each base prime,
13	for a certificate over `Localization.Away r` of an adaptation of the **pulled** system
14	`d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away r))`.  Every support/no-leak/clopen lemma of
15	the lane, however, is stated for a system on `relCurve C R`.  Composing the two needs the
16	transport recorded here: the support locus of a pulled system is the preimage of the support
17	locus.
18	
19	Both inclusions come from the same fact: `f.stalkMap z` is a **local** ring homomorphism
20	(`AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyRingedSpace.isLocalHomStalkMap`), so it both preserves and
21	reflects unit-ness, and the germ of a pulled equation is the `stalkMap` image of the germ of
22	the original (`germ_appLE_apply`, re-derived here since it is `private` upstream).
23	
24	## Main declarations
25	
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.unitLocus_pullback` — the unit locus pulls back.
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.supportLocus_pullback` — the support locus pulls
28	  back; the hinge the certificate lane needs.
29	-/
30	
31	set_option autoImplicit false
32	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
33	
34	universe u
35	
36	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
37	
38	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
39	
40	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
41	
42	variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
43	
44	/-- The germ of a pulled-back equation is the `stalkMap` image of the germ of the original.
45	(The upstream `germ_appLE_apply` is `private`; this is the instance of it the transport
46	needs, spelled for `pullbackEqn`.) -/
47	lemma germ_pullbackEqn_eq_stalkMap (f : Y ⟶ X) (E : X.LocalEquations) (y : Y)
48	    {z : Y} (hz : z ∈ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y) :
49	    (Y.presheaf.germ ((E.cover.pullback f).opens y) z hz).hom (pullbackEqn f E y)
50	      = (f.stalkMap z).hom
51	        ((X.presheaf.germ (E.cover.opens (f.base y)) (f.base z)
52	          (by exact hz)).hom (E.eqn (f.base y))) := by
53	  simp only [pullbackEqn, Scheme.Hom.appLE, CommRingCat.comp_apply,
54	    Scheme.Hom.germ_stalkMap_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
55	
56	/-- **The unit locus pulls back.** A point of `Y` is in the unit locus of the pulled system
57	exactly when its image is in the unit locus of the original: the germ of the pulled equation
58	is the `stalkMap` image of the germ of the original, and `stalkMap` is a local hom, so it
59	preserves and reflects unit-ness. -/
60	theorem unitLocus_pullback (f : Y ⟶ X) (E : X.LocalEquations) (hreg) :
61	    ((E.pullback f hreg).unitLocus : Set Y) = f.base ⁻¹' (E.unitLocus : Set X) := by
62	  ext z
63	  have hzmem : z ∈ (E.pullback f hreg).cover.opens z := (E.cover.pullback f).mem_opens z
64	  have hfz : f.base z ∈ E.cover.opens (f.base z) := E.cover.mem_opens (f.base z)
65	  rw [Set.mem_preimage, SetLike.mem_coe, SetLike.mem_coe,
66	    (E.pullback f hreg).mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hzmem,
67	    E.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hfz]
68	  have hgerm : (Y.presheaf.germ ((E.pullback f hreg).cover.opens z) z hzmem).hom
69	      ((E.pullback f hreg).eqn z)
70	      = (f.stalkMap z).hom
71	        ((X.presheaf.germ (E.cover.opens (f.base z)) (f.base z) hfz).hom
72	          (E.eqn (f.base z))) :=
73	    germ_pullbackEqn_eq_stalkMap f E z hzmem
74	  rw [hgerm]
75	  exact ⟨fun hu => isUnit_of_map_unit (f.stalkMap z).hom _ hu,
76	    fun hu => hu.map (f.stalkMap z).hom⟩
77	
78	/-- **The support locus pulls back** — the hinge of the certificate lane: it lets every
79	support/no-leak/clopen statement proved for a system on `relCurve C R` be read on the pulled
80	system over an `Away` chart, which is what the pointwise gate consumes. -/
81	theorem supportLocus_pullback (f : Y ⟶ X) (E : X.LocalEquations) (hreg) :
82	    (E.pullback f hreg).supportLocus = f.base ⁻¹' E.supportLocus := by
83	  rw [supportLocus, supportLocus, unitLocus_pullback f E hreg, Set.preimage_compl]
84	
85	end Scheme.LocalEquations
86	
87	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# The certificate of a support-separated adaptation
11	
12	The DD-R certificate lane was built around the equalizer `W(d) = ker (δ_left − δ_right)`
13	of the two overlap-restriction arrows.  Its two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4), and the
14	kernel-spanning input of `isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`, are the genuinely hard
15	relative content — `DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean` shows the kernel-spanning law is
16	*equivalent* to the flatness one is trying to prove, so no cleverer submodule evades it.
17	
18	This file records the escape hatch that the *pointwise* gate opens up.  Because
19	`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation` accepts **any**
20	adaptation over the shrunken base, we are free to choose one whose pieces are
21	**support-separated**: each off-diagonal overlap misses the divisor, so its overlap
22	colength vanishes.  For such an adaptation
23	
24	* `δ_left = δ_right` on the nose (`deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated`), hence
25	* `W(d)` is the whole product `∏_j colength j` (`gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'`), and
26	* both cokernels are *zero* modules, so (c3)/(c4) hold for free
27	  (`flat_coker_incl_of_separated`, `flat_coker_diff_of_separated`).
28	
29	What remains of the certificate is only the (c1) data — chart-local colengths finite
30	projective — plus the constant-rank reading of their product.  Both are already available:
31	(c1) from the support tube (`SupportTubeFinite.lean`, `SupportTube.lean`) and the rank as a
32	sum of the per-piece ranks (`Module.rankAtStalk_pi`).
33	
34	This is a genuine reduction, not a repackaging: the hypothesis it trades for is the
35	*geometric separation* of the chosen pieces, which the tube produces one base point at a
36	time, whereas the discharged hypotheses were fibrewise flatness statements over a
37	nonreduced base.
38	
39	## Main declarations
40	
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'` — the equalizer
42	  collapses over an arbitrary base ring (the field-level lemma generalized).
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated` — the Čech
44	  difference vanishes.
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_separated` — the certificate from
46	  (c1) plus a rank reading, with no kernel-spanning and no flatness input.
47	-/

63	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
64	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
65	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
66	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
67	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)
68	
69	omit [IsProper C.hom]

71	/-- On the diagonal the two overlap-restriction maps coincide: the two `≤`-witnesses
72	`pieces i ⊓ pieces i ≤ pieces i` are definitionally equal (proof irrelevance).  The
73	base-ring form of `DivisorFamilyFieldDegree`'s field-level lemma. -/
74	lemma toOvlLeft_self_eq_toOvlRight_self' (i : A.index) :
75	    A.toOvlLeft i i = A.toOvlRight i i :=
76	  rfl
77	
78	/-- **Support separation collapses the equalizer to the whole product, over any base
79	ring.** If the overlap colength modules vanish off the diagonal, every element of the
80	product of chart-local colengths satisfies the equalizer condition.
81	
82	The field-level statement (`gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated`) never used invertibility;
83	this is the same argument over `R`, which is what the DD-R gate consumes. -/
84	lemma gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'
85	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
86	    A.gluedSubmodule = ⊤ := by
87	  refine eq_top_iff.mpr fun s _ => ?_
88	  rw [mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
89	  rintro ⟨i, j⟩
90	  by_cases hij : i = j
91	  · subst hij
92	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun f : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i i => (f : _ → _))
93	      (A.toOvlLeft_self_eq_toOvlRight_self' i)) (s i)
94	  · haveI := hsep i j hij
95	    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
96	
97	/-- **The Čech difference vanishes for a support-separated adaptation.** Its kernel is the
98	whole product, and a linear map whose kernel is everything is zero. -/
99	lemma deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated
100	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
101	    A.deltaLeft = A.deltaRight := by
102	  have h : A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight = 0 := by
103	    rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_top]
104	    exact A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated' hsep
105	  exact sub_eq_zero.mp h
106	
107	/-- The equalizer, as a module, is the whole product of chart-local colengths. -/
108	noncomputable def gluedTopEquiv' (h : A.gluedSubmodule = ⊤) : A.Glued ≃ₗ[R] A.chartProd :=
109	  (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ h).trans Submodule.topEquiv
110	
111	/-! ## The two flat-cokernel clauses, for free -/
112	
113	/-- (c3) for a support-separated adaptation: the cokernel of `W(d) ↪ ∏_j colength j` is the
114	zero module, because the inclusion is onto. -/
115	lemma flat_coker_incl_of_separated
116	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
117	    Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule) := by
118	  haveI : Subsingleton (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule) := by
119	    rw [A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated' hsep]
120	    infer_instance
121	  exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv
122	    (N := A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule) (M := PUnit.{u+1})
123	    (LinearEquiv.ofSubsingleton _ _)
124	
125	/-- (c4) for a support-separated adaptation: the Čech difference is the zero map, so its
126	range is `⊥` and the cokernel is the overlap product itself — flat as soon as the overlap
127	product is.  In the seed setting that flatness is already landed
128	(`flat_ovlProd_of_seed`). -/
129	lemma flat_coker_diff_of_separated [Module.Flat R A.ovlProd]
130	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
131	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)) := by
132	  have hzero : A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight = 0 :=
133	    sub_eq_zero.mpr (A.deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated hsep)
134	  rw [hzero, LinearMap.range_zero]
135	  exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv (Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot ⊥ rfl)
136	
137	/-! ## Separation is a statement about the support, not about the equations
138	
139	The hypothesis `hsep` above is checkable geometrically: an overlap whose points all avoid
140	the family support carries a unit equation, hence a unit overlap ideal, hence a vanishing
141	overlap colength.  In particular an adaptation in which **at most one piece meets the
142	support** is automatically separated. -/
143	
144	/-- **Overlaps that miss the support are separated.** If no point of `pieces i ⊓ pieces j`
145	lies in the support locus, then `A.eqn i` restricts to a unit there (its germ is a unit at
146	every point, `RingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ`), so the overlap ideal is the unit ideal
147	and the overlap colength vanishes. -/
148	lemma subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus (i j : A.index)
149	    (hdisj : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
150	    Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j) := by
151	  have hunit : IsUnit (relResAlgHom C R
152	      (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)) := by
153	    rw [relResAlgHom_apply]
154	    apply (relCurve C R).toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
155	    intro z hz
156	    rw [(relCurve C R).presheaf.germ_res_apply]
157	    have hU : z ∈ d.unitLocus := not_not.mp (hdisj z hz)
158	    exact (A.isUnit_germ_eqn_iff i hz.1).mpr
159	      ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens z)).mp hU)
160	  have htop : A.ovlIdeal i j = ⊤ :=
161	    Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ (Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)) hunit
162	  exact Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr htop
163	
164	/-- **One support-meeting piece suffices.** If every piece other than `j₀` avoids the
165	support entirely, the adaptation is separated: any off-diagonal overlap involves a piece
166	missing the support, so the overlap misses it too. -/
167	lemma forall_subsingleton_ovlColength_of_unique_support_piece (j₀ : A.index)
168	    (hother : ∀ j : A.index, j ≠ j₀ →
169	      ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
170	    ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j) := by
171	  intro i j hij
172	  refine A.subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus i j fun z hz => ?_
173	  by_cases hi : i = j₀
174	  · exact hother j (by rw [← hi]; exact fun h => hij h.symm) z hz.2
175	  · exact hother i hi z hz.1
176	
177	/-! ## The scope guard: separation forces a fibre-confined support
178	
179	The converse direction bounds this route honestly.  Both pinned charts carry a partition
180	of unity, so a support point lying in `V₀ ⊓ V₁` lies in a piece of **each** chart — an
181	off-diagonal pair whose overlap then meets the support.  Hence a separated adaptation
182	exists only for a system whose support avoids the chart overlap, i.e. is confined to the
183	two vertical fibres of `pi`.  No refinement of the cover repairs this, and the pointwise
184	gate does not help: shrinking the base deletes fibres, it does not move a support point
185	out of `V₀ ⊓ V₁`.
186	
187	The field lane recorded the same obstruction and routed around it
188	(`DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean`, deviation note): over a field every module is free, so the
189	certificate is discharged on the plain extraction adaptation instead.  Over a nonreduced
190	base that escape is unavailable, which is exactly why the flat-cokernel content of
191	`DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean` is unavoidable for a general degree-`g` system. -/
192	
193	/-- **Separation confines the support to the chart overlap's complement.** If a support
194	point `z` lies in both pinned charts, the chart-0 pieces cover `V₀` and the chart-1 pieces
195	cover `V₁`, so `z` lies in a chart-0 piece `i` and a chart-1 piece `j`; these are distinct
196	(`Sum.inl ≠ Sum.inr`), and both equations have non-unit germ at `z`, so the overlap ideal
197	is proper and `ovlColength i j` is **not** subsingleton.
198	
199	So `isCertified_of_separated` applies only to fibre-confined systems.  It is stated to
200	record the scope of the separated route, not to suggest the hypothesis is generic. -/
201	theorem supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated
202	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j))
203	    {z : relCurve C R} (hz : z ∈ d.supportLocus)
204	    (hz₀ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₀)
205	    (hz₁ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₁) : False := by
206	  classical
207	  -- the two charts' partitions of unity put `z` in a piece of each chart
208	  obtain ⟨i₀, hi₀⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (A.toFinCoverData.cover₀ hz₀)
209	  obtain ⟨j₀, hj₀⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (A.toFinCoverData.cover₁ hz₁)
210	  set i : A.index := Sum.inl i₀ with hi
211	  set j : A.index := Sum.inr j₀ with hj
212	  have hzi : z ∈ A.pieces i := hi₀
213	  have hzj : z ∈ A.pieces j := hj₀
214	  -- the germs of both equations at `z` are non-units, since `z` is in the support
215	  have hnu : ∀ l : A.index, ∀ hzl : z ∈ A.pieces l,
216	      ¬ IsUnit (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces l) z hzl).hom (A.eqn l)) := by
217	    intro l hzl hu
218	    exact hz ((A.mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus l hzl).mp
219	      (((relCurve C R).mem_basicOpen (A.eqn l) z hzl).mpr hu))
220	  -- but separation makes the overlap colength trivial, i.e. the overlap ideal is `⊤`
221	  haveI := hsep i j (by simp [hi, hj])
222	  have htop : A.ovlIdeal i j = ⊤ := Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mp ‹_›
223	  -- evaluating `1 ∈ ovlIdeal i j` at the germ of `z` contradicts non-unitness
224	  have hzW : z ∈ A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j := ⟨hzi, hzj⟩
225	  have hone : (1 : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j)) ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j := by
226	    rw [htop]; exact Submodule.mem_top
227	  rw [Ideal.mem_span_pair] at hone
228	  obtain ⟨a, b, hab⟩ := hone
229	  -- push the identity into the local ring at `z`
230	  have hgerm := congrArg
231	    (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) z hzW).hom) hab
232	  rw [map_one, map_add, map_mul, map_mul] at hgerm
233	  -- both germ images lie in the maximal ideal, so their combination cannot be `1`
234	  have hmi : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) z hzW).hom
235	      (relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i))
236	      ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
237	    rw [relResAlgHom_apply, (relCurve C R).presheaf.germ_res_apply]
238	    exact not_not.mp (fun h => hnu i hzi (IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal.mp h))
239	  have hmj : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) z hzW).hom
240	      (relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j))
241	      ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
242	    rw [relResAlgHom_apply, (relCurve C R).presheaf.germ_res_apply]
243	    exact not_not.mp (fun h => hnu j hzj (IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal.mp h))
244	  have hmem : (1 : (relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z)
245	      ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
246	    rw [← hgerm]
247	    exact Ideal.add_mem _ (Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ hmi) (Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ hmj)
248	  exact (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z)).ne_top_iff_one.mp
249	    (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal.isMaximal _).ne_top hmem
250	
251	/-- **"At most one piece meets the support" is impossible once the support meets both
252	pinned charts.** This refutes, at the level of the pieces, the shape the `tube-fibre` leaf
253	of the certificate lane was aiming at.
254	
255	A support point `z` of `V₀ ⊓ V₁` lies in a chart-0 piece and a chart-1 piece, and those are
256	distinct — so two distinct pieces meet the support, no matter how the cover is refined. -/
257	theorem not_exists_unique_support_piece
258	    {z : relCurve C R} (hz : z ∈ d.supportLocus)
259	    (hz₀ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₀)
260	    (hz₁ : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover pi)).V₁)
261	    (j₀ : A.index)
262	    (hother : ∀ j : A.index, j ≠ j₀ →
263	      ∀ y : relCurve C R, y ∈ A.pieces j → y ∉ d.supportLocus) : False :=
264	  A.supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated
265	    (A.forall_subsingleton_ovlColength_of_unique_support_piece j₀ hother) hz hz₀ hz₁
266	
267	/-! ## The certificate -/
268	
269	/-- **The certificate of a support-separated adaptation.** With the off-diagonal overlap
270	colengths vanishing, the equalizer is the whole product, the Čech difference is zero, and
271	both flat-cokernel clauses hold automatically.  What is left is exactly the (c1) data —
272	each chart-local colength finite projective over `R` — plus the constant-rank reading,
273	which for the product is the sum of the per-piece ranks.
274	
275	This is the shape the pointwise gate can consume: no kernel-spanning hypothesis, and no
276	flatness of a Čech cokernel over a possibly nonreduced base. -/
277	theorem isCertified_of_separated {n : ℕ} [Module.Flat R A.ovlProd]
278	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j))
279	    (hfin : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j))
280	    (hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j))
281	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
282	      ∑ᶠ j : A.index, Module.rankAtStalk (R := R) (A.colength j) p = n) :
283	    A.IsCertified n := by
284	  classical
285	  haveI := hfin
286	  haveI := hproj
287	  haveI : ∀ j : A.index, Module.Flat R (A.colength j) := fun _ =>
288	    Module.Flat.of_projective
289	  have htop := A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated' hsep
290	  have hequiv : A.Glued ≃ₗ[R] A.chartProd := A.gluedTopEquiv' htop
291	  haveI hprodProj : Module.Projective R A.chartProd :=
292	    Module.Projective.of_equiv' (P := A.chartProd)
293	      (DirectSum.linearEquivFunOnFintype R A.index (fun j => A.colength j))
294	  refine
295	    { finite_colength := hfin
296	      projective_colength := hproj
297	      finite_glued := Module.Finite.equiv hequiv.symm
298	      projective_glued := Module.Projective.of_equiv' (P := A.Glued) hequiv.symm
299	      rankAtStalk_glued := fun p => ?_
300	      flat_coker_incl := A.flat_coker_incl_of_separated hsep
301	      flat_coker_diff := A.flat_coker_diff_of_separated hsep }
302	  rw [Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv hequiv, Module.rankAtStalk_pi]
303	  exact hrank p
304	
305	end DivisorAdaptation

13	/-!
14	# Fibrewise avoidance by a coordinate twist
15	
16	Over an infinite ground field, the image in `P¹` of a finite divisor fibre misses two members of
17	the pencil `X₁ - aX₀`. The associated `GL₂` coordinate change puts the fibre inside the overlap of
18	the two twisted affine charts. Properness then spreads this confinement to a Zariski neighbourhood
19	of the base point.
20	
21	The finiteness hypothesis is explicit: `LocalEquations` does not itself package the support as a
22	finite morphism. Callers must obtain fibre finiteness from their geometric divisor data, not from a
23	certificate.
24	-/
25	
26	set_option autoImplicit false
27	set_option quotPrecheck false
28	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
29	set_option maxRecDepth 16000

41	/-! ## Finite support on a curve -/
42	
43	/-- A regular local-equation system on a smooth integral quasi-compact curve over a field has
44	finite support. Its support is contained in the finite order support of its meromorphic
45	presentation; regularity excludes the generic point. -/
46	theorem supportLocus_finite_on_curve (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
47	    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
48	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
49	    [IsIntegral X] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
50	    (d : X.LocalEquations) : d.supportLocus.Finite := by
51	  let T : Set {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X} :=
52	    {p | Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) p.2
53	      (d.presentation.elem p.1) ≠ 1}
54	  have hT : T.Finite := d.presentation.ordZ_elem_support_finite K
55	  refine (hT.image Subtype.val).subset ?_
56	  intro x hx
57	  have hxg : x ≠ genericPoint X := by
58	    intro h
59	    subst x
60	    have hnot := (d.mem_supportLocus_iff_not_isUnit_germ
61	      (d.cover.mem_opens (genericPoint X))).mp hx
62	    apply hnot
63	    exact isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr (mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_ne_zero.mp
64	      (d.regular (genericPoint X) (genericPoint X)
65	        (d.cover.mem_opens (genericPoint X))))
66	  refine ⟨⟨x, hxg⟩, ?_, rfl⟩
67	  change Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hxg
68	    (d.presentation.elem x) ≠ 1
69	  intro hord
70	  have hnot := (d.mem_supportLocus_iff_not_isUnit_germ
71	    (d.cover.mem_opens x)).mp hx
72	  apply hnot
73	  exact (Scheme.isUnit_germ_iff_ordZ_eq_one K
74	    (d.cover.genericPoint_mem_opens x) (d.eqn x)
75	    (d.presentation.elem x) (d.presentation_elem_val x)
76	    (d.cover.mem_opens x) hxg).mpr hord
77	
78	/-- Away from the generic point, the support locus of regular local equations is exactly the
79	support of the associated presentation divisor. -/
80	theorem mem_supportLocus_iff_mem_presentationDivisor_support
81	    (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
82	    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
83	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
84	    [IsIntegral X] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
85	    (d : X.LocalEquations) {x : X} (hxg : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
86	    x ∈ d.supportLocus ↔
87	      (⟨x, hxg⟩ : {y : X // y ≠ genericPoint X}) ∈
88	        (toFinsupp (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation)).support := by
89	  rw [Finsupp.mem_support_iff]
90	  change x ∈ d.supportLocus ↔
91	    coeffAt hxg (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation) ≠ 0
92	  rw [Scheme.coeffAt_presentationDivisor,
93	    d.mem_supportLocus_iff_not_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens x),
94	    Scheme.isUnit_germ_iff_ordZ_eq_one K
95	      (d.cover.genericPoint_mem_opens x) (d.eqn x)
96	      (d.presentation.elem x) (d.presentation_elem_val x)
97	      (d.cover.mem_opens x) hxg]
98	  simp
99	
100	/-- Regular local equations do not vanish at the generic point. -/
101	theorem genericPoint_not_mem_supportLocus
102	    (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
103	    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
104	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
105	    [IsIntegral X] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
106	    (d : X.LocalEquations) : genericPoint X ∉ d.supportLocus := by

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

/-! ## The flatness ladder: section rings of basic opens are flat over the test ring -/

section BasicOpenFlat

variable (K : Type u) [CommRing K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]

/-- **Flatness descends to basic opens**: for an affine open `V` with `Γ(X, V)` flat over
the base ring `K`, the section ring of any basic open `D(f) ⊆ V` is flat over `K` —
`Γ(X, D(f))` is a localization of `Γ(X, V)` (`IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen`),
localizations are flat, and flatness composes along the scalar tower
`K → Γ(X, V) → Γ(X, D(f))`. -/
theorem flat_sections_basicOpen {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (hflat : Module.Flat K Γ(X, V)) (f : Γ(X, V)) :
    Module.Flat K Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) := by
  haveI := hflat
  haveI := hV.isLocalization_basicOpen f
  haveI : Module.Flat Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) :=
    IsLocalization.flat _ (Submonoid.powers f)
  haveI : IsScalarTower K Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) :=
    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun r =>
      (X.overAlgebraMap_apply_res K (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le f)).op r).symm
  exact Module.Flat.trans K Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f)

end BasicOpenFlat

/-! ## Section-level and unit-ratio consequences of germwise regularity -/

section GermRegular

lemma relPinnedChart_true :
    relPinnedChart C R π true = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := rfl

/-- Both pinned charts are affine. -/
lemma isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart (b : Bool) : IsAffineOpen (relPinnedChart C R π b) := by
  cases b
  · exact relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)
  · exact relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)

/-- **Flatness of the pinned chart sections over the test ring**: `Γ(C_R, Vᵢᴿ)` is the
free base change `R ⊗[k] Γ(C, Vᵢ)` (`free_relSections`), hence flat. -/
theorem flat_sections_relPinnedChart (b : Bool) :
    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) := by
  cases b
  · haveI : Module.Free R Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π false) :=
      free_relSections C R (fiberChart₀ π)
        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).isCompact
        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).isQuasiSeparated
    exact Module.Flat.of_free
  · haveI : Module.Free R Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π true) :=
      free_relSections C R (fiberChart₁ π)
        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).isCompact
        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).isQuasiSeparated
    exact Module.Flat.of_free

/-- Two distinct members of the pencil `X₁ - aX₀` are the rows of an invertible matrix. -/
theorem exists_matrix_twistedCoord_eq (a b : k) (hab : a ≠ b) :
    ∃ M : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) k,
      twistedCoord k M 0 = X 1 - C a * X 0 ∧
      twistedCoord k M 1 = X 1 - C b * X 0 := by
  let A : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) k := !![-a, 1; -b, 1]
  have hdet : Matrix.det A ≠ 0 := by
    rw [show Matrix.det A = b - a by
      simp [A, Matrix.det_fin_two_of, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm]]
    exact sub_ne_zero.mpr (Ne.symm hab)
  let M : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) k :=
    Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.mkOfDetNeZero A hdet
  refine ⟨M, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [twistedCoord, MvPolynomial.matrixLinearForm, M, A, Fin.sum_univ_two,
      MvPolynomial.smul_eq_C_mul, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm]
  · simp [twistedCoord, MvPolynomial.matrixLinearForm, M, A, Fin.sum_univ_two,
      MvPolynomial.smul_eq_C_mul, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm]

/-- Over a finite field with at least two more elements than `S`, one coordinate twist puts
the finite subset `S` inside the intersection of the two twisted standard charts. -/
theorem exists_matrix_finite_subset_chartInter_of_ncard_add_two_le [Fintype k]
    (S : Set (P1 k)) (hS : S.Finite) (hcard : S.ncard + 2 ≤ Fintype.card k) :
    ∃ M : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) k,
      S ⊆ ((autOfMatrix k M ⁻¹ᵁ chartOpen k 0 : (P1 k).Opens) : Set (P1 k)) ∩
        ((autOfMatrix k M ⁻¹ᵁ chartOpen k 1 : (P1 k).Opens) : Set (P1 k)) := by
  classical
  let B : Set k := ⋃ x ∈ S, badScalars k x
  have hB : B.Finite := by
    dsimp [B]
    exact hS.biUnion fun x _ => (badScalars_subsingleton k x).finite
  have hBncard : B.ncard ≤ S.ncard := by
    dsimp [B]
    exact badScalars_biUnion_ncard_le k S hS
  let s : Finset k := hB.toFinset
  have hs : 1 < sᶜ.card := by
    rw [Finset.card_compl]
    have hscard : s.card = B.ncard := (Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card B hB).symm
    omega
  obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hab⟩ := Finset.one_lt_card.mp hs
  have haB : a ∉ B := by simpa [s] using ha
  have hbB : b ∉ B := by simpa [s] using hb
  obtain ⟨M, hM0, hM1⟩ := exists_matrix_twistedCoord_eq k a b hab
  refine ⟨M, fun x hx => ?_⟩
  constructor
  · rw [autOfMatrix_preimage_chartOpen]
    change twistedCoord k M 0 ∉ x.asHomogeneousIdeal
    rw [hM0]
    intro hbad
    apply haB
    exact Set.mem_iUnion_of_mem x (Set.mem_iUnion_of_mem hx hbad)
  · rw [autOfMatrix_preimage_chartOpen]
    change twistedCoord k M 1 ∉ x.asHomogeneousIdeal
    rw [hM1]
    intro hbad
    apply hbB
    exact Set.mem_iUnion_of_mem x (Set.mem_iUnion_of_mem hx hbad)

/-- Over an infinite field, one coordinate twist puts any finite subset of `P¹` inside the
intersection of the two twisted standard charts. -/
theorem exists_matrix_finite_subset_chartInter [Infinite k]
    (S : Set (P1 k)) (hS : S.Finite) :
    ∃ M : Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) k,
      S ⊆ ((autOfMatrix k M ⁻¹ᵁ chartOpen k 0 : (P1 k).Opens) : Set (P1 k)) ∩
        ((autOfMatrix k M ⁻¹ᵁ chartOpen k 1 : (P1 k).Opens) : Set (P1 k)) := by
  let B : Set k := ⋃ x ∈ S, badScalars k x
  have hB : B.Finite := by
    dsimp [B]
    exact hS.biUnion fun x _ => (badScalars_subsingleton k x).finite
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hB.exists_notMem
  have hBa : (B ∪ {a}).Finite := hB.union (Set.finite_singleton a)

/-- **The colength certificate** (worksheet §1.1 (c1)/(c2) in the spec-dd-1 §1c frozen
spelling): chart-local colengths finite projective over `R` (c1); the glued module
finite projective of constant fibre rank `n` — honest finrank at every prime through
`Module.rankAtStalk` (c2); and the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
certificates base-change along ARBITRARY test maps (trivial over a field; transported
by right-exactness; consumed by `FlatCokernel.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`). -/
structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
  flat_coker_diff :
    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))

scheme is *clopen* in that scheme.  The following two lemmas identify that principle with the
leak locus, so the two vocabularies are the same statement:

the piece trace `supp ∩ U` is always **open** in the subspace `supp` (as `U` is open), so it
is clopen there precisely when it is closed in the ambient space — precisely when nothing
leaks. -/

/-- **Leak-freeness is clopen-ness of the trace in the support.** The forward direction of
the identification with the Z-clopen principle (I-0209). -/
theorem isClopen_trace_of_supportLeak_eq_empty (U : X.Opens)
    (h : d.supportLeak U = ∅) :
    IsClopen ((fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (U : Set X)) := by
  have hclosed : IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X)) :=
    (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty U).mpr h
  refine ⟨?_, U.isOpen.preimage continuous_subtype_val⟩
  have heq : (fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (U : Set X)
      = (fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X)) := by
    ext x; simp
  rw [heq]
  exact hclosed.preimage continuous_subtype_val

/-- The converse, from the closedness half alone: a trace closed in the support leaks
nothing.  (The openness half is automatic — see `supportLeak_eq_empty_iff_isClosed_trace`
for the honest equivalence.) -/
theorem supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isClopen_trace (U : X.Opens)
    (h : IsClosed ((fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (U : Set X))) :
    d.supportLeak U = ∅ := by
  refine (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty U).mp ?_
  -- a set closed in the closed subspace `supp` is closed in `X`
  obtain ⟨T, hT, hTeq⟩ := (isClosed_induced_iff (f := fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val)).mp h
  have heq : d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X) = d.supportLocus ∩ T := by
    ext x
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨hxs, hxU⟩
      exact ⟨hxs, (Set.ext_iff.mp hTeq ⟨x, hxs⟩).mpr hxU⟩
    · rintro ⟨hxs, hxT⟩
      exact ⟨hxs, (Set.ext_iff.mp hTeq ⟨x, hxs⟩).mp hxT⟩
  rw [heq]
  exact d.isClosed_supportLocus.inter hT

/-- **The honest equivalence.** Leak-freeness at `U` is exactly closedness of the piece
trace in the subspace `supp` — and since that trace is *always* open there (`U` is open), it
is exactly clopen-ness of the trace, i.e. the Z-clopen condition of I-0209.

The `IsClopen` spelling of the forward direction (`isClopen_trace_of_supportLeak_eq_empty`)
carries a free rider: the openness half holds unconditionally, so the content of the
identification is this `Iff` on the closedness half. -/
theorem supportLeak_eq_empty_iff_isClosed_trace (U : X.Opens) :
    d.supportLeak U = ∅ ↔
      IsClosed ((fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (U : Set X)) :=
  ⟨fun h => (d.isClopen_trace_of_supportLeak_eq_empty U h).1,
    d.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isClopen_trace U⟩

/-- The piece trace is always **open** in the support, with no hypothesis — the half of
clopen-ness that carries no information. -/
theorem isOpen_trace (U : X.Opens) :
    IsOpen ((fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (U : Set X)) :=
  U.isOpen.preimage continuous_subtype_val

end Scheme.LocalEquations

section RelCurveFlat

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]

/-- **The relative curve is flat over its test base.** `(snd C (overSpec k R)).left` is the
base change of `C.hom` along `(overSpec k R).hom` (`Over.isPullback_left`), and every
structure morphism to the spectrum of a field is flat (`flat_hom_over_field`). -/
instance instFlatRelCurveHom : AlgebraicGeometry.Flat (relCurve C R ↘ Spec (.of R)) :=
  AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.isStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback
    (Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k R)) inferInstance

/-- **Flat sections on an arbitrary affine open of the relative curve** — the widened
(c1)-flatness input, with no chart and no freeness. -/
theorem flat_sections_isAffineOpen {V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, V) :=
  flat_sections_of_flat_hom R (relCurve C R) hV

end RelCurveFlat

/-! ## The widened cover datum -/

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)

/-- **The widened cover datum** (R2, human decision I-0492): finitely many **arbitrary
affine opens** of the relative curve that **jointly** cover it.

Contrast with `FinCoverData`, which this replaces on the certificate side: there is no `h₀`,
no `h₁`, no `a₀`/`a₁`, no `partition₀`/`partition₁`, no `Sum` index, and above all no typing
of a piece into a pinned chart.  The chart-wise partitions of unity are exactly what upgraded
per-piece swallow-or-miss to a chart statement, and they are gone deliberately; the two-chart
structure the Θ-layer needs is carried separately (see `ChartTyping` below), never by the
certificate clauses.

`Type u`, like `FinCoverData`, so a functor value can quotient it. -/
structure AffCoverData : Type u where
  /-- The number of pieces. -/
  m : ℕ
  /-- The pieces: arbitrary opens of the relative curve, made affine by `isAffineOpen`. -/
  pieces : Fin m → (relCurve C R).Opens
  /-- Every piece is affine — the only geometric demand the certificate layer makes. -/
  isAffineOpen : ∀ j, IsAffineOpen (pieces j)
  /-- The pieces cover the curve JOINTLY.  This replaces the two chart-wise partitions of
  unity, and it is the whole structural content of the widening. -/
  cover : (⨆ j, pieces j) = ⊤

namespace AffCoverData

variable {C R π} (D : AffCoverData C R)

/-- The gluing index of the widened datum: a bare `Fin`, with no two-sided structure. -/
abbrev index : Type := Fin D.m

/-- **Every point lies in a piece.** Under `FinCoverData` this came from `relCover_sup`
together with the two partitions of unity; here it is exactly the joint covering field —
obligation I-0492 4(ii) discharged in one line rather than silently supplied by the typing. -/
lemma exists_mem_pieces (z : relCurve C R) : ∃ j : D.index, z ∈ D.pieces j := by
  have hz : z ∈ (⨆ j, D.pieces j) := by rw [D.cover]; trivial
  exact Opens.mem_iSup.mp hz

/-- The pieces are affine opens — by fiat now, rather than as basic opens of an affine
chart. -/
lemma isAffineOpen_pieces (j : D.index) : IsAffineOpen (D.pieces j) :=
  D.isAffineOpen j

/-- **Flatness of the piece section rings over the test ring.** The widened replacement for
`FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces`, which localized a FREE pinned-chart ring; here it is the
flat structure morphism of the relative curve read on an affine open. -/
theorem flat_sections_pieces (j : D.index) :
    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) :=
  flat_sections_isAffineOpen C R (D.isAffineOpen j)
